31	## `record_screen`
32	
33	Records for a set number of seconds and lands the result as ordinary media, as **File ▸ New Recording…** does without the panel. It records a display or a window, the microphone alone, or a camera alone, and it can record a camera beside the screen. [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/) has the whole story. See also [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).
34	
35	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
36	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
37	| `seconds` | number | Yes | How long to record, 1 to 600. |
38	| `source` | string | No | `screen` (the default), `voice_over` for the default microphone alone, or `camera` for a camera alone. |
39	| `display` | integer | No | Which display, with 0 the main one. Default: 0. Not with `window`. |
40	| `window` | integer | No | A window's id, to record that window on its own at its own size. Not with `display`. |
41	| `size` | string | No | `nominal` (the default) records the display's point size, and `best` its pixel size. |
42	| `rate` | integer | No | The capture's frame rate, 30 or 60. Default: 60. It's also the canvas rate of a new project the recording opens as. |
43	| `system_audio` | boolean | No | Captures what every application but Frame Job plays, as the movie's stereo 48 kHz track. Default: true. |
44	| `microphone` | boolean | No | Records the default microphone to a second file beside the movie. Default: false. |
45	| `show_clicks` | boolean | No | Shows each mouse click. With `cursor` `separate`, the clips land with click ripples. With `in_picture`, a circle goes into the movie. Default: false. |
46	| `cursor` | string | No | `separate` keeps the pointer out of the movie and Frame Job draws it, and `in_picture` burns it in. Default: `separate`. |
47	| `keys` | string | No | `off` (the default), or `shortcuts` to write each shortcut pressed and a time-only mark for every other key into the cursor file, never which key was typed. Needs the Input Monitoring grant. |
48	| `include_framejob_windows` | boolean | No | Puts Frame Job's own windows in a display recording. Default: false. |
49	| `camera` | string | No | With `source` `camera`, the camera to record alone. Default: the system's preferred camera, else the first built-in, else the first. With `source` `screen`, a camera to record beside the screen. Default: none. A device's unique id, or its name in any case. |
50	| `camera_format` | string | No | The format, such as `1920x1080@30`, or `WIDTHxHEIGHT` for that size's highest rate, or `best`. Default: `best`. |
51	| `camera_layout` | string | No | With a camera beside the screen, where it lands: `corner_square` (the default, bottom right), `corner_rounded`, `corner_circle`, `side_by_side` or `camera_full`. |
52	| `camera_cutout` | boolean | No | With a camera beside the screen, runs Remove Background on the camera clips as its own undo step. Default: false. |
53	| `enhance` | boolean | No | Runs `enhance_voice` on the microphone's clips once their sound is analysed, as its own undo step. Default: false. |
54	| `auto_zoom` | boolean | No | Runs [`auto_zoom`](#auto_zoom) on the screen clips as its own undo step. Default: false. |
55	| `shortcut_overlays` | boolean | No | Runs [`add_shortcut_overlays`](#add_shortcut_overlays) on the screen clips, after `auto_zoom`, as its own undo step. Needs `keys: "shortcuts"`. Default: false. |
56	| `speed_up_typing` | boolean | No | Runs [`speed_up_typing`](#speed_up_typing) on the screen clips, last, once their speech is detected, as its own undo step. Needs `keys: "shortcuts"`. Default: false. |
57	| `place` | boolean | No | Puts the clips on the timeline at the playhead, in one undo step with the media. `false` adds the media and no clip, except in a new project, whose first picture is the document. Default: true. |
58	| `path` | string | No | A folder to record into, made if it doesn't exist. Default: `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`. It names the folder, never the file. |
59	
60	Only some of these go together:
61	
62	| With | Frame Job won't take |
63	| --- | --- |
64	| `source: "voice_over"` | `display`, `window`, `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows`, `keys`, `cursor`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, any `camera` argument, or `microphone: false` |
65	| `source: "camera"` | `display`, `window`, `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows`, `keys`, `cursor`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, `camera_layout`, `camera_cutout` or `rate` |
66	| `source: "screen"` with no `camera` | `camera_format`, `camera_layout` or `camera_cutout` |
67	| `place: false` | `enhance`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, `camera_layout` or `camera_cutout` |
68	
69	`enhance` also needs `microphone: true` or a voice-over.
70	
71	The call blocks for the whole recording, then until the files are closed and landed. If the files are slow to close it waits up to 75 s, and 60 s more for each further segment of a paused recording, or 105 s and 90 s with a camera beside the screen. `enhance` and `speed_up_typing` each wait up to 5 minutes more for the analysis they need. It answers `path`, `media`, `clip`, `duration`, `width`, `height`, `fps`, `has_audio`, `audio_tracks`, `mic_offset`, `pauses`, `segments` with one entry for each file, `stopped_by` and `landed`, plus the microphone's and the camera's own keys when they're used, and a `note` when there's something to say. Each polish step adds its own answer under its name, or a sentence under `<name>_error`, such as `auto_zoom_error`.
72	
73	A person at the Mac can pause, resume and stop an agent's recording from the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or the **File** menu. A pause shortens what's recorded, because `seconds` is wall-clock time, and a stop ends it early and it still lands.
74	
75	**It never asks for a grant.** The Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera and Input Monitoring grants must already be held. A missing one is refused by name, with its System Settings pane, or, for a Microphone or Camera grant macOS hasn't asked about yet, with **File ▸ New Recording…** as the place to give it. The recorder panel is where a person gives them. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/). Frame Job started from a shell runs under the terminal's grants, not the app's. The [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-can-do/) can't use this tool, so it's for a client connected over MCP.
76	
77	It checks in a fixed order: your own arguments with the Microphone and Input Monitoring grants first, then the camera, its format and the Camera grant, then the Screen Recording grant, then the display or window. A locked console or sleeping displays are refused as that, by name. An unknown camera or format is refused naming what's there.

79	## `set_media_cursor`
80	
81	Attaches, moves or removes a screen recording's cursor file, the `.fjcursor` Frame Job writes beside each recorded movie. It's **Locate…** and **Remove** in the Media tab's **Cursor** section. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/).
82	
83	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
84	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
85	| `media` | integer | Yes | The video media's id. |
86	| `cursor` | object | Yes | `{path, bookmark?, in_picture}`, the media's `cursor` as `get_project` shows it, or null to forget the file. The file itself stays on disk. |
87	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to make the edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
88	
89	Give `path` in full, because `~` isn't expanded here. `in_picture` says whether the movie's picture already shows the pointer, and it must match the file.
90	
91	It answers as an edit does, with `media` added, and it's one undo step, **Locate Cursor File** or **Remove Cursor File**. **Consolidate Media** copies the file into the package beside its movie, and opening a moved package finds it there.
92	
93	It won't attach the file when:
94	
95	- `path` is empty.
96	- The file doesn't open as a cursor file.
97	- The file was made for a movie of a different size.
98	- `in_picture` isn't the file's own.
99	- The media isn't a video with a picture.

101	## `get_cursor_events`
102	
103	Reads what a recording's cursor file holds: its clicks, scrolls, shortcuts, stretches of typing and, if asked, the pointer's path. It runs on your Mac, needs no key, edits nothing and makes no undo step. There's no menu for it. See [What a cursor file holds](/recording/cursor-files/#what-a-cursor-file-holds).
104	
105	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
106	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
107	| `media` | integer | One of these | The recording, read in the file's own source ticks. |
108	| `clip` | integer | One of these | A media clip of a recording, read in ticks from the clip's start, through its speed and ramps. |
109	| `from` | integer | No | Where to start, in ticks, in the answer's time. Default: 0. |
110	| `to` | integer | No | Where to stop, not included, in ticks. Must be after `from`. Default: the media's or the clip's duration. |
111	| `kinds` | array of strings | No | Any of `clicks`, `scrolls`, `shortcuts`, `typing` and `path`. Default: the first four. |
112	| `smoothing` | number | No | The path's smoothing, 0 to 1. Default: the clip's own **Smoothing** in its Cursor section, else 0, the raw path. |
113	
114	It answers `ok`, `time` (`media` or `clip`), `from`, `to`, `count`, `media`, `clip` when given, `size` as `[w, h]`, `cursor_file`, `in_picture`, a `project` summary, and one key for each kind asked for:
115	
116	| Key | What it holds |
117	| --- | --- |
118	| `clicks` | A list of `{t, button, down, count, x, y}`. `button` is 0 left, 1 right, 2 other. `down` is 1 for a press and 0 for a release. |
119	| `scrolls` | A list of `{t, x, y, dx, dy}`, each a single wheel event, with `dx` and `dy` in points. |
120	| `shortcuts` | A list of `{t, keys, code}`. |
121	| `typing` | A list of `{from, to, marks}`, each stretch that overlaps the window. |
122	| `path` | `{smoothing, t, x, y}`, sampled 10 times a second. |
123	
124	`x` and `y` are the movie's own pixels from its top left.
125	
126	**Zoom on a click.** With `clip`, each click and scroll also has `q`, as `[qx, qy]`: its position as an offset in source pixels from the centre of the clip's cropped picture. That's the frame `add_zoom_action`'s region takes, so a region around a click is `{x: qx, y: qy, width, height}`. See [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/).
127	
128	**Long recordings.** Rows of every kind and path samples count together, and an answer holds at most 5,000. `next` is then the first time left out, so call again with `from: next`.
129	
130	It won't read when:
131	
132	- It doesn't get exactly one of `media` and `clip`.
133	- `kinds` is empty or names something else, or `smoothing` is outside 0 to 1.
134	- `to` isn't after `from`.
135	- The clip isn't a media clip, or it plays reversed. Ask with its media instead.
136	- The media has no cursor file, or the file is missing.

138	## `auto_zoom`
139	
140	Plans screencast zooms from the clicks and typing in a recording's cursor file, and applies them as one undo step, **Auto Zoom**. It's **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**. See [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/).
141	
142	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
143	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
144	| `clip` | integer | One of these | A screen recording's media clip. |
145	| `clips` | array of integers | One of these | Media clips whose media have cursor files. |
146	| `zoom` | number | No | How far in, times the clip's own scale: 1.25 to 4. Default: 2. |
147	| `lead` | number | No | Arrive this many seconds before the click: 0.2 to 2. Default: 0.6. |
148	| `stay` | number | No | Stay this many seconds after the last activity: 0.5 to 10. Default: 2.5. |
149	| `follow` | boolean | No | Follows the pointer while zoomed. Default: true. |
150	| `typing` | boolean | No | Zooms on stretches of typing too. Default: true. |
151	| `replace` | boolean | No | Removes the clips' existing zooms first. Default: false. |
152	| `motion_blur` | number | No | The shutter given to each zoomed clip whose own `motion_blur` is 0, as a fraction of a frame: 0 to 1. Default: 0.5, a 180° shutter. 0 sets none. |
153	| `from` | integer | No | Plans only clicks and typing at or after this time, in ticks. With `replace`, removes only zooms that meet the `from` to `to` window. |
154	| `to` | integer | No | Plans only before this time, in ticks. |
155	
156	Each zoom is an ordinary action, the shape `add_zoom_action` makes, so it can be edited like any other. A visit starts at a click, or at a stretch of typing aimed at the last click before it. It zooms in `lead` seconds before that and back out over 0.8 seconds, `stay` seconds after the last activity. [How a visit is planned](/recording/auto-zoom/#how-a-visit-is-planned) has the rest.
157	
158	Halves of a split are planned as one, and nothing straddles a cut. See [Across a split](/recording/auto-zoom/#across-a-split). A planned zoom that meets an action already on the clip is dropped. `replace` removes only zooms, never any other action. A clip that already has a shutter keeps it.
159	
160	It answers as an edit does, and adds:
161	
162	| Key | What it holds |
163	| --- | --- |
164	| `visits` | How many visits were planned. |
165	| `added`, `replaced`, `dropped` | Zooms added, existing zooms removed, and planned zooms dropped because they met an action. |
166	| `closed_at_cut` | Visits closed at a cut, because the later half wasn't named in the call or has an action of its own there. |
167	| `bases_set` | Later halves whose base was set, by a zoom held across a cut or by `replace` putting it back. |
168	| `blurred` | How many clips were given `motion_blur`. |
169	| `actions` | A list of `{clip, at, duration, kind}`, with `at` in clip ticks and `kind` one of `in`, `pan`, `follow` or `back`. |
170	
171	Besides [the shared rules](#the-tools-that-work-from-a-cursor-file), it won't run when a number is out of range, a clip has no picture, or a clip is placed smaller than the canvas. For that last one, nest the clip, open the nest with `set_scope` and call `auto_zoom` inside it.

173	## `add_shortcut_overlays`
174	
175	Places one Keyboard keys graphic clip for each keyboard shortcut recorded, at the moment it was pressed, as one undo step, **Add Shortcut Overlays**. It's **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays**, which has no sheet, so an agent is the only way to choose these settings. See [Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/).
176	
177	Only shortcuts are recorded, never typed keys, and only when the recording was made with **Record shortcuts** or `keys: "shortcuts"`. See [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/).
178	
179	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
180	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
181	| `clip` | integer | One of these | A screen recording's media clip. |
182	| `clips` | array of integers | One of these | Media clips whose media have cursor files. |
183	| `duration` | number | No | How long each overlay shows, in seconds: 0.5 to 10. Default: 1.5. |
184	| `position` | string | No | Where the keycaps sit: `bottom` (the default), `center` or `top`. |
185	| `theme` | string | No | The keycaps' look: `dark` (the default) or `light`. |
186	| `from` | integer | No | Places only shortcuts at or after this time, in ticks. |
187	| `to` | integer | No | Places only shortcuts before this time, in ticks. |
188	
189	An overlay never lasts less than 10 frames for each keycap plus 25, the time the template needs to press its last key and exit. Overlays never overlap:
190	
191	- The same shortcut pressed again before its overlay ends extends it, labelled ×2, ×3 and so on.
192	- A different shortcut pressed sooner ends the earlier overlay where it starts, once the earlier one has had its minimum. If that puts it more than 0.5 seconds after its press, it's dropped.
193	
194	The clips go on the front-most track named **Shortcuts** when it's in front of every clip's track, unlocked, shown, not a matte and free over their span. Otherwise they go on a new **Shortcuts** track at the front. A module in `graphics/` whose text equals the bundled template is reused, and otherwise the template is copied in once, only when something is placed.
195	
196	The overlays are ordinary graphic clips. See [Change an overlay](/recording/shortcut-overlays/#change-an-overlay).
197	
198	It answers as an edit does, and adds:
199	
200	| Key | What it holds |
201	| --- | --- |
202	| `added`, `merged`, `dropped` | Overlays placed, repeat presses folded into one, and presses left out. |
203	| `track`, `new_track` | The track used, and whether it's new. |
204	| `module`, `written` | The module drawn, and whether the template was copied in. |
205	| `overlays` | A list of `{at, duration, keys, label}`, with `at` in timeline ticks. |
206	
207	Besides [the shared rules](#the-tools-that-work-from-a-cursor-file), it won't run with a `duration`, `position` or `theme` out of range.
208	
209	## `speed_up_typing`
210	
211	Plays the typing in screen recordings faster, keeping speech and shortcuts at normal speed, as one undo step, **Speed Up Typing**. It's **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…**. See [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/).
212	
213	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
214	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
215	| `clip` | integer | One of these | A screen recording's media clip. |
216	| `clips` | array of integers | One of these | Media clips whose media have cursor files. Halves of a split recording are joined. |
217	| `rate` | number | No | How much faster a stretch plays: 2 to 8. Default: 4. |
218	| `shortest` | number | No | The shortest stretch sped up, in seconds: 1 to 30. Default: 3. |
219	| `keep_pitch` | boolean | No | Keeps the sped sound's pitch. Default: true. |
220	| `from` | integer | No | Speeds only typing at or after this time, in ticks. |
221	| `to` | integer | No | Speeds only typing before this time, in ticks. |
222	
223	A typing stretch is a run of at least 3 typed keys, each under 1 second apart. Taken out of each stretch are every span of speech, in any clip with sound under it on any track, and each recorded shortcut with its overlay, which is 1.5 seconds when it has no clip on a **Shortcuts** track. The pieces of all the clips join where they meet, and a piece shorter than `shortest` is left alone.
224	
225	Each kept piece is sped by `retime_range` at `rate` on every unlocked track, keeping 0.3 seconds at normal speed at each end, so everything after it moves up in step. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
226	
227	Speech detection runs on your Mac. A media with sound under a stretch that has no speech saved yet gets its spans in the same step.
228	
229	It answers `ok`, a `project` summary and the ids it created, and adds:
230	
231	| Key | What it holds |
232	| --- | --- |
233	| `stretches`, `short` | Stretches sped up, and pieces left alone for being too short. |
234	| `ranges` | A list of `{from, to, sped_to}`, in timeline ticks before the edit. |
235	| `saved` | The time saved, in ticks. |
236	| `speech_saved` | The media whose speech was saved in this step. |
237	| `audio_left_out`, `audio_note` | Only when a clip with sound now plays past ×12, the ceiling for sound. Unlike the menu command, it doesn't ask. See [If a clip would go silent](/recording/speed-up-typing/#if-a-clip-would-go-silent). |
238	
239	Besides [the shared rules](#the-tools-that-work-from-a-cursor-file), it won't run, and nothing changes, when:
240	
241	- `rate` or `shortest` is out of range.
242	- `retime_range` would refuse any range, because of a locked track after it, a transition or a linked clip, for example. The sentence names it.
243	- Speech detection is still running. It doesn't wait, and it says to try again in a moment.

2	title: "Tools: rendering and export"
3	description: "The agent tools that render one frame of the timeline, start an export, follow it on the Export Queue and stop it."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These tools turn the timeline into pictures and files. `render_frame` is how an agent sees what it has done, and `export`, `export_status` and `cancel_export` write the finished file.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['File ▸ Save Frame…', 'File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
12	  keys="⌘E"
13	  tools={['render_frame', 'export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
14	  needs="A client connected over MCP, or the Assistant tab."
15	/>
16	
17	Each tool has a heading here with its arguments. [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/) and [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/) walk through using them.
18	
19	Every tool here also takes `project`, the path of an open project. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/). None of them takes `scope`.
20	
21	## `render_frame`
22	
23	Renders one frame of the finished timeline as a picture the model can see and a file on disk. It goes through the same composition and compositor an export does, so it shows what the file will hold at that moment. Use it before and after every edit. It's the same writer as **File ▸ Save Frame…**, so a PNG written here and one saved from the menu are byte-identical. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).
24	
25	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
26	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
27	| `t` | integer | No | The moment to render, in ticks, rounded to the frame grid. Default: the playhead. |
28	| `path` | string | No | Where to write the file. The folder must exist. Default: a temporary file. |
29	| `format` | string | No | `png`, `jpeg` or `heic`. Default: the path's own extension when it's one of those, else `png`. An explicit format wins, and the path's extension is replaced, so `shot.jpg` with `png` writes `shot.png`. |
30	| `max_width` | integer | No | Caps the image's width, 16 to 8192 pixels, aspect kept and never scaled up. Default: the canvas's own size. |
31	| `burn_in_timecode` | boolean | No | Draws the project timecode over the picture, topmost. Default: false. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
32	| `ungraded` | boolean | No | Draws as if no clip were graded, which is **View ▸ Show Ungraded**'s picture. Default: false. See [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/). |
33	| `sdr_version` | boolean | No | Draws an HDR project's SDR version, which is **View ▸ Show SDR Version**'s picture. An SDR project's frame doesn't change. Default: false. See [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/). |
34	| `selection` | integer | No | An adjustment clip's id. Draws what its qualifier selects, which is **View ▸ Show Selection**'s picture: grey, white fully graded and black untouched, with every layer in front of the clip left out. Black where the clip isn't on the frame. See [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/). |
35	| `waveform` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's luma waveform. Default: false. |
36	| `parade` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's RGB parade. Default: false. |
37	| `vectorscope` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's vectorscope. Default: false. |
38	| `vectorscope_zoom` | integer | No | The vectorscope's zoom: 1, 2 or 4. Needs `vectorscope: true`. Default: 1. |
39	| `histogram` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's histogram. Default: false. |
40	
41	The view switches themselves never reach this tool, so an agent asks for each picture here, whatever a person has switched on.
42	
43	It answers an image block and a text block. The text says the moment, the canvas's size and the size it rendered at, and its last sentence is "Written to `<path>`." Before that last sentence it can add:
44	
45	- A note that a JPEG flattened a transparent canvas onto black. PNG and HEIC keep the canvas's transparency.
46	- A graphic that warned or failed, naming it, its frame and the problem. A failed graphic draws its error card in the picture.
47	- A recorded cursor that couldn't be drawn: "The cursor of media M is not drawn:" and why. The clip draws without one.
48	- A clip with Remove Background whose masks weren't ready. It waits up to 30 seconds, then draws the clip uncut and names it.
49	- What each scope measured.
50	
51	**Scopes.** Each scope you ask for adds a sentence and writes a JSON file beside the image, named `<image path>.waveform.json`, `.parade.json`, `.vectorscope.json` or `.histogram.json`. The waveform and histogram sentences give the share of pixels clipping high and low, the parade gives it for each channel, and the vectorscope gives the share that's neutral. The waveform, parade and vectorscope count into 256 × 256 bins, and the histogram into 256 levels. At zoom 2 or 4, pixels off the vectorscope's plot aren't counted, and the text says what share they are. See [Scopes](/color/scopes/).
52	
53	**In an HDR project,** the frame is a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC labelled BT.2100 HLG. A JPEG, and any frame asked for with `sdr_version`, is the project's SDR version, labelled BT.709. Scopes read the picture drawn, so the HLG signal adds `signal: "hlg"` to each JSON file.
54	
55	**With a nest open,** it renders that nest, at its own canvas and from its own zero, which is what the preview is showing. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
56	
57	It won't render when:
58	
59	- `selection` isn't an adjustment clip of the project.
60	- `vectorscope_zoom` isn't 1, 2 or 4, or comes without `vectorscope: true`.
61	- `max_width` or `format` is out of range, `path` is empty, or the folder doesn't exist.
62	- There's no frame at that time, because it's past the end, the media is missing or the timeline is empty.
63	
64	## `export`
65	
66	Puts the timeline on the Export Queue and answers at once, as **File ▸ Export…** (<kbd>⌘E</kbd>) does with its sheet. It takes everything on the sheet but the frame rate: an export runs at the project's rate, or at 12.5 fps for `gif` and 25 fps for `apng`. An agent's export and a menu export go through the same exporter. See [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/).
67	
68	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
69	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
70	| `preset` | string | Yes | The encoding, one of the [presets](#the-presets). A wrong one is refused with the full list. |
71	| `path` | string | Yes | Where to write. The folder must exist. The format's extension is added when the path has none, and an existing file is replaced. |
72	| `size` | string or array of 2 integers | No | The sheet's **Size**: `document`, `2160p`, `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p`, `preset` (`gif` and `apng` only), or `[width, height]` in pixels, 16 to 8192 on each edge. Default: the document's size, or the format's cap on `gif` and `apng`. See [Export size](/export/size/). |
73	| `range` | string | No | `project` (the default) for the whole timeline, or `in_out` for the range `set_range` set. |
74	| `video_bitrate` | integer | No | Target video rate in bits per second, 1 or more, so 8000000 is 8 Mbps. Default: the preset decides. ProRes, `gif` and `apng` ignore it, and on AV1 and VP9 it's a soft cap. See [Export quality](/export/quality/). |
75	| `audio_bitrate` | integer | No | Target AAC or Opus rate in bits per second, 1 or more. Default: 192 kbps. ProRes, WAV and AIFF ignore it. |
76	| `audio_bits` | integer | No | `audio_wav`'s and `audio_aiff`'s bit depth, 16 or 24. Default: 16. Refused on every other preset. See [Export bit depth](/export/bit-depth/). |
77	| `loudness_lufs` | number | No | Normalises the whole mix to this integrated loudness, −70 to 0 LUFS. The sheet's rows are −14, −16 and −23. Omit it not to normalise. Ignored by `gif` and `apng`. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/). |
78	| `peak_dbtp` | number | No | The ceiling of the master limiter every export with sound runs, −20 to 0 dBTP. Default: −1. There's no off. |
79	| `burn_in_timecode` | boolean | No | Draws the project timecode over the picture. It shows project time even in a range export. Default: false. |
80	| `dynamic_range` | string | No | An HDR project's picture on `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422` and `prores_4444`: `hlg` (the default), `pq` for HDR10, or `sdr`. Every other video preset writes the SDR version. See [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/). |
81	| `encoder_speed` | string | No | `av1`'s and `av1_webm`'s speed: `faster`, `balanced` (the default) or `smaller`. Refused on every other preset. See [Encoder speed](/export/encoder-speed/). |
82	| `stems` | string | No | Also writes stems beside the mix on the three audio presets: `tracks` for one file per heard track, or `names` for one per track name. See [Audio stems](/export/stems/). |
83	
84	### The presets
85	
86	A preset is a container and a codec, with no size of its own, except that `gif` and `apng` each have a cap.
87	
88	| Preset | Writes | Good to know |
89	| --- | --- | --- |
90	| `h264` | H.264 in MP4 | 8-bit. What the export sheet opens on. |
91	| `hevc` | HEVC in MP4 | 8-bit. |
92	| `hevc_alpha` | HEVC with alpha in MOV | 8-bit. Keeps a transparent canvas. Safari's transparent movie. |
93	| `hevc_10bit` | HEVC in MP4 | 10-bit. |
94	| `av1` | AV1 in MP4 with AAC | 10-bit. Macs before M3 can't play it back. |
95	| `av1_webm` | AV1 in WebM with Opus | 10-bit. Macs before M3 can't play it back. |
96	| `vp9_webm` | VP9 in WebM with Opus | 8-bit for an SDR picture, 10-bit for HLG and PQ. |
97	| `vp9_alpha_webm` | VP9 with alpha in WebM with Opus | Always 8-bit. Keeps a transparent canvas. The transparent movie Chrome and Firefox play. |
98	| `prores_422` | ProRes 422 in MOV | 10-bit. |
99	| `prores_4444` | ProRes 4444 in MOV | 12-bit. Keeps a transparent canvas. |
100	| `audio_m4a` | AAC in M4A | Sound only. |
101	| `audio_wav` | WAV | Sound only. |
102	| `audio_aiff` | AIFF | Sound only. |
103	| `gif` | Animated GIF | Can show a transparent pixel, but nothing partial survives. |
104	| `apng` | Animated PNG | Keeps a transparent canvas. |
105	
106	See [Choose a format](/export/formats/) for what each is for.
107	
108	### What it answers
109	
110	`export` answers `{export_id, path, status}` at once, and `status` is `queued` or `running`. The job runs one at a time behind any other export already on the queue. An `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` or `vp9_alpha_webm` job also waits while the app's other AV1 and VP9 exports would hold more than a quarter of this Mac's memory with it, and a later job may run first meanwhile. The queue window isn't opened. The export always writes the whole document, even with a nest open.
111	
112	Follow it with [`export_status`](#export_status) and stop it with [`cancel_export`](#cancel_export). The `export_id` lasts until Frame Job quits.
113	
114	### When it refuses
115	
116	Every refusal comes back from this call, before anything is queued. `export` won't start when:
117	
118	- There's nothing on the timeline.
119	- `range` is `in_out` and the project has no in and out range.
120	- `preset` is unknown, or `size` isn't a row or a pair of edges from 16 to 8192. Each sentence lists what it takes.
121	- `size` is `preset` on anything but `gif` or `apng`.
122	- `audio_bits` or `encoder_speed` is on a preset that doesn't take it.
123	- `dynamic_range` is `hlg` or `pq` on a video preset that can't write it, or on any video preset in an SDR project, where `sdr` changes nothing. An audio preset ignores it.
124	- `stems` is on a movie preset, or no track can be heard.
125	- The folder doesn't exist.
126	- A graphic clip's module doesn't compile.
127	
128	A failure while writing comes back from `export_status` instead. That includes a `[width, height]` more than a pixel off the canvas's shape on `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha` or `vp9_alpha_webm`, because padding would destroy the alpha those presets are chosen for. It also includes a graphic that fails during the export, which stops it with no file left and names the graphic and the frame, and a stem whose file would replace media the project uses.
129	
130	## `export_status`
131	
132	Answers how an export is going. It's the job's row in **Window ▸ Export Queue**, read now. It never waits, so call it again after a pause until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
133	
134	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
135	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
136	| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` answered, 1 or more. |
137	
138	Every answer has `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed`, the seconds since `export` was called, or up to the finish once it has finished. The rest depends on `status`:
139	
140	| Status | Adds |
141	| --- | --- |
142	| `queued` | `waiting`, the queue row's sentence, while the job waits for memory behind other AV1 and VP9 exports. |
143	| `queued` or `running` | `estimated_seconds` on `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`: the export sheet's estimate of the whole write, in whole seconds. |
144	| `running` | `progress`, 0 to 1, and `phase` while the exporter names one, such as the loudness measurement. |
145	| `done` | What the file holds, below. |
146	| `failed`, `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
147	
148	When it's `done`, it adds:
149	
150	| Key | What it holds |
151	| --- | --- |
152	| `ok`, `bytes` | True, and the file's size. |
153	| `preset`, `container`, `codec`, `width`, `height`, `fps`, `start`, `duration` | The settings used. `fps` is `[num, den]`, and the width and height are the file's. |
154	| `burn_in_timecode` | Whether the burn-in was asked for. |
155	| `dynamic_range` | In an HDR project, the picture written. |
156	| `encoder_speed` | On `av1` and `av1_webm`. |
157	| `audio_bits` | On `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. |
158	| `stems` | With `stems`, a list of `{name, tracks, path}`, one for each file beside the mix. |
159	| `loudness` | For every format that carries sound, normalised or not: `summary`, `integrated_lufs`, `true_peak_dbtp`, `sample_peak_dbfs`, `gain_db`, `ceiling_dbtp`, `limited_db`, `capped_by_gain`, and `target_lufs` when one was asked for. Absent when there was no sound to measure. |
160	| `graphic_warnings` | A list of `{name, frame, message}`, each distinct warning a graphic gave while the file was drawn. Absent when there were none. |
161	| `cursor_warnings` | A list of `{media, path, message}`, each media whose cursor file couldn't be drawn, so its clips drew without one. Absent when there were none. |
162	
163	`integrated_lufs` is absent for a programme too short or too quiet to have one, and `summary` says so in words. `limited_db` says how far the limiter turned the hottest peak down, and `capped_by_gain` is true when the +40 dB gain cap decided the gain.
164	
165	Only ids `export` answered since Frame Job launched are known. Anything else is refused, and that includes a job a person put on the queue. A finished job's answer outlives its queue row, so it still reads after **Remove** or **Clear Finished**.
166	
167	## `cancel_export`
168	
169	Stops an export, as **Cancel** in its Export Queue row does. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
170	
171	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
172	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
173	| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` answered, 1 or more. |
174	
175	A queued export is cancelled before it starts. A running one stops and its half-written file is removed, though the answer may still read `running` until the writer has stopped, when `export_status` reads `cancelled`. A finished export is left alone.
176	
177	It answers as `export_status` does, and it refuses an id `export` didn't answer since launch.
178	
179	## Related
180	
181	- [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/)
182	- [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/)
183	- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)
184	- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)

1	---
2	title: "Tools: recording and screencasts"
3	description: "The agent tools that record the screen, a camera or the microphone, read and attach cursor files, and add zooms, shortcut overlays and faster typing to a screencast."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These tools make a recording and then polish it as a screencast. `record_screen` records. The rest read the cursor file Frame Job writes beside a screen recording, and use what it holds to zoom on clicks, show shortcuts and speed through typing.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['File ▸ New Recording…', 'Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…', 'Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays', 'Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…']}
12	  where="Media tab ▸ Cursor"
13	  tools={['record_screen', 'set_media_cursor', 'get_cursor_events', 'auto_zoom', 'add_shortcut_overlays', 'speed_up_typing']}
14	  needs="Recording needs its system grants, which only a person can give. The rest runs on your Mac with no key."
15	/>
16	
17	Every tool here also takes `project`, the path of an open project. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/). Times are in ticks, 600,000 a second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
18	
19	## The tools that work from a cursor file
20	
21	`auto_zoom`, `add_shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` share these rules:
22	
23	- Each takes exactly one of `clip` and `clips`.
24	- `from` and `to` are in the time of the timeline or nest that's open, and `to` must be after `from`. The menu commands can't limit themselves this way.
25	- None takes `scope`. Each acts in whatever `set_scope` has open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
26	- None remembers the settings a person last used in a sheet. They start from the defaults below.
27	- With nothing to do, each answers `ok` with a `note` and makes no undo step.
28	
29	Each one won't run when a clip isn't a media clip, its media has no cursor file or the file is missing, or it plays reversed. If the project changes while the cursor files are read, the call changes nothing and says to call again.
30	
31	## `record_screen`
32	
33	Records for a set number of seconds and lands the result as ordinary media, as **File ▸ New Recording…** does without the panel. It records a display or a window, the microphone alone, or a camera alone, and it can record a camera beside the screen. [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/) has the whole story. See also [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).
34	
35	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
36	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
37	| `seconds` | number | Yes | How long to record, 1 to 600. |
38	| `source` | string | No | `screen` (the default), `voice_over` for the default microphone alone, or `camera` for a camera alone. |
39	| `display` | integer | No | Which display, with 0 the main one. Default: 0. Not with `window`. |
40	| `window` | integer | No | A window's id, to record that window on its own at its own size. Not with `display`. |
41	| `size` | string | No | `nominal` (the default) records the display's point size, and `best` its pixel size. |
42	| `rate` | integer | No | The capture's frame rate, 30 or 60. Default: 60. It's also the canvas rate of a new project the recording opens as. |
43	| `system_audio` | boolean | No | Captures what every application but Frame Job plays, as the movie's stereo 48 kHz track. Default: true. |
44	| `microphone` | boolean | No | Records the default microphone to a second file beside the movie. Default: false. |
45	| `show_clicks` | boolean | No | Shows each mouse click. With `cursor` `separate`, the clips land with click ripples. With `in_picture`, a circle goes into the movie. Default: false. |
46	| `cursor` | string | No | `separate` keeps the pointer out of the movie and Frame Job draws it, and `in_picture` burns it in. Default: `separate`. |
47	| `keys` | string | No | `off` (the default), or `shortcuts` to write each shortcut pressed and a time-only mark for every other key into the cursor file, never which key was typed. Needs the Input Monitoring grant. |
48	| `include_framejob_windows` | boolean | No | Puts Frame Job's own windows in a display recording. Default: false. |
49	| `camera` | string | No | With `source` `camera`, the camera to record alone. Default: the system's preferred camera, else the first built-in, else the first. With `source` `screen`, a camera to record beside the screen. Default: none. A device's unique id, or its name in any case. |
50	| `camera_format` | string | No | The format, such as `1920x1080@30`, or `WIDTHxHEIGHT` for that size's highest rate, or `best`. Default: `best`. |
51	| `camera_layout` | string | No | With a camera beside the screen, where it lands: `corner_square` (the default, bottom right), `corner_rounded`, `corner_circle`, `side_by_side` or `camera_full`. |
52	| `camera_cutout` | boolean | No | With a camera beside the screen, runs Remove Background on the camera clips as its own undo step. Default: false. |
53	| `enhance` | boolean | No | Runs `enhance_voice` on the microphone's clips once their sound is analysed, as its own undo step. Default: false. |
54	| `auto_zoom` | boolean | No | Runs [`auto_zoom`](#auto_zoom) on the screen clips as its own undo step. Default: false. |
55	| `shortcut_overlays` | boolean | No | Runs [`add_shortcut_overlays`](#add_shortcut_overlays) on the screen clips, after `auto_zoom`, as its own undo step. Needs `keys: "shortcuts"`. Default: false. |
56	| `speed_up_typing` | boolean | No | Runs [`speed_up_typing`](#speed_up_typing) on the screen clips, last, once their speech is detected, as its own undo step. Needs `keys: "shortcuts"`. Default: false. |
57	| `place` | boolean | No | Puts the clips on the timeline at the playhead, in one undo step with the media. `false` adds the media and no clip, except in a new project, whose first picture is the document. Default: true. |
58	| `path` | string | No | A folder to record into, made if it doesn't exist. Default: `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`. It names the folder, never the file. |
59	
60	Only some of these go together:
61	
62	| With | Frame Job won't take |
63	| --- | --- |
64	| `source: "voice_over"` | `display`, `window`, `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows`, `keys`, `cursor`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, any `camera` argument, or `microphone: false` |
65	| `source: "camera"` | `display`, `window`, `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows`, `keys`, `cursor`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, `camera_layout`, `camera_cutout` or `rate` |
66	| `source: "screen"` with no `camera` | `camera_format`, `camera_layout` or `camera_cutout` |
67	| `place: false` | `enhance`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, `camera_layout` or `camera_cutout` |
68	
69	`enhance` also needs `microphone: true` or a voice-over.
70	
71	The call blocks for the whole recording, then until the files are closed and landed. If the files are slow to close it waits up to 75 s, and 60 s more for each further segment of a paused recording, or 105 s and 90 s with a camera beside the screen. `enhance` and `speed_up_typing` each wait up to 5 minutes more for the analysis they need. It answers `path`, `media`, `clip`, `duration`, `width`, `height`, `fps`, `has_audio`, `audio_tracks`, `mic_offset`, `pauses`, `segments` with one entry for each file, `stopped_by` and `landed`, plus the microphone's and the camera's own keys when they're used, and a `note` when there's something to say. Each polish step adds its own answer under its name, or a sentence under `<name>_error`, such as `auto_zoom_error`.
72	
73	A person at the Mac can pause, resume and stop an agent's recording from the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or the **File** menu. A pause shortens what's recorded, because `seconds` is wall-clock time, and a stop ends it early and it still lands.
74	
75	**It never asks for a grant.** The Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera and Input Monitoring grants must already be held. A missing one is refused by name, with its System Settings pane, or, for a Microphone or Camera grant macOS hasn't asked about yet, with **File ▸ New Recording…** as the place to give it. The recorder panel is where a person gives them. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/). Frame Job started from a shell runs under the terminal's grants, not the app's. The [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-can-do/) can't use this tool, so it's for a client connected over MCP.
76	
77	It checks in a fixed order: your own arguments with the Microphone and Input Monitoring grants first, then the camera, its format and the Camera grant, then the Screen Recording grant, then the display or window. A locked console or sleeping displays are refused as that, by name. An unknown camera or format is refused naming what's there.
78	
79	## `set_media_cursor`
80	
81	Attaches, moves or removes a screen recording's cursor file, the `.fjcursor` Frame Job writes beside each recorded movie. It's **Locate…** and **Remove** in the Media tab's **Cursor** section. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/).
82	
83	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
84	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
85	| `media` | integer | Yes | The video media's id. |
86	| `cursor` | object | Yes | `{path, bookmark?, in_picture}`, the media's `cursor` as `get_project` shows it, or null to forget the file. The file itself stays on disk. |
87	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to make the edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
88	
89	Give `path` in full, because `~` isn't expanded here. `in_picture` says whether the movie's picture already shows the pointer, and it must match the file.
90	
91	It answers as an edit does, with `media` added, and it's one undo step, **Locate Cursor File** or **Remove Cursor File**. **Consolidate Media** copies the file into the package beside its movie, and opening a moved package finds it there.
92	
93	It won't attach the file when:
94	
95	- `path` is empty.
96	- The file doesn't open as a cursor file.
97	- The file was made for a movie of a different size.
98	- `in_picture` isn't the file's own.
99	- The media isn't a video with a picture.
100	
101	## `get_cursor_events`
102	
103	Reads what a recording's cursor file holds: its clicks, scrolls, shortcuts, stretches of typing and, if asked, the pointer's path. It runs on your Mac, needs no key, edits nothing and makes no undo step. There's no menu for it. See [What a cursor file holds](/recording/cursor-files/#what-a-cursor-file-holds).
104	
105	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
106	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
107	| `media` | integer | One of these | The recording, read in the file's own source ticks. |
108	| `clip` | integer | One of these | A media clip of a recording, read in ticks from the clip's start, through its speed and ramps. |
109	| `from` | integer | No | Where to start, in ticks, in the answer's time. Default: 0. |
110	| `to` | integer | No | Where to stop, not included, in ticks. Must be after `from`. Default: the media's or the clip's duration. |
111	| `kinds` | array of strings | No | Any of `clicks`, `scrolls`, `shortcuts`, `typing` and `path`. Default: the first four. |
112	| `smoothing` | number | No | The path's smoothing, 0 to 1. Default: the clip's own **Smoothing** in its Cursor section, else 0, the raw path. |
113	
114	It answers `ok`, `time` (`media` or `clip`), `from`, `to`, `count`, `media`, `clip` when given, `size` as `[w, h]`, `cursor_file`, `in_picture`, a `project` summary, and one key for each kind asked for:
115	
116	| Key | What it holds |
117	| --- | --- |
118	| `clicks` | A list of `{t, button, down, count, x, y}`. `button` is 0 left, 1 right, 2 other. `down` is 1 for a press and 0 for a release. |
119	| `scrolls` | A list of `{t, x, y, dx, dy}`, each a single wheel event, with `dx` and `dy` in points. |
120	| `shortcuts` | A list of `{t, keys, code}`. |
121	| `typing` | A list of `{from, to, marks}`, each stretch that overlaps the window. |
122	| `path` | `{smoothing, t, x, y}`, sampled 10 times a second. |
123	
124	`x` and `y` are the movie's own pixels from its top left.
125	
126	**Zoom on a click.** With `clip`, each click and scroll also has `q`, as `[qx, qy]`: its position as an offset in source pixels from the centre of the clip's cropped picture. That's the frame `add_zoom_action`'s region takes, so a region around a click is `{x: qx, y: qy, width, height}`. See [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/).
127	
128	**Long recordings.** Rows of every kind and path samples count together, and an answer holds at most 5,000. `next` is then the first time left out, so call again with `from: next`.
129	
130	It won't read when:
131	
132	- It doesn't get exactly one of `media` and `clip`.
133	- `kinds` is empty or names something else, or `smoothing` is outside 0 to 1.
134	- `to` isn't after `from`.
135	- The clip isn't a media clip, or it plays reversed. Ask with its media instead.
136	- The media has no cursor file, or the file is missing.
137	
138	## `auto_zoom`
139	
140	Plans screencast zooms from the clicks and typing in a recording's cursor file, and applies them as one undo step, **Auto Zoom**. It's **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**. See [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/).
141	
142	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
143	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
144	| `clip` | integer | One of these | A screen recording's media clip. |
145	| `clips` | array of integers | One of these | Media clips whose media have cursor files. |
146	| `zoom` | number | No | How far in, times the clip's own scale: 1.25 to 4. Default: 2. |
147	| `lead` | number | No | Arrive this many seconds before the click: 0.2 to 2. Default: 0.6. |
148	| `stay` | number | No | Stay this many seconds after the last activity: 0.5 to 10. Default: 2.5. |
149	| `follow` | boolean | No | Follows the pointer while zoomed. Default: true. |
150	| `typing` | boolean | No | Zooms on stretches of typing too. Default: true. |
151	| `replace` | boolean | No | Removes the clips' existing zooms first. Default: false. |
152	| `motion_blur` | number | No | The shutter given to each zoomed clip whose own `motion_blur` is 0, as a fraction of a frame: 0 to 1. Default: 0.5, a 180° shutter. 0 sets none. |
153	| `from` | integer | No | Plans only clicks and typing at or after this time, in ticks. With `replace`, removes only zooms that meet the `from` to `to` window. |
154	| `to` | integer | No | Plans only before this time, in ticks. |
155	
156	Each zoom is an ordinary action, the shape `add_zoom_action` makes, so it can be edited like any other. A visit starts at a click, or at a stretch of typing aimed at the last click before it. It zooms in `lead` seconds before that and back out over 0.8 seconds, `stay` seconds after the last activity. [How a visit is planned](/recording/auto-zoom/#how-a-visit-is-planned) has the rest.
157	
158	Halves of a split are planned as one, and nothing straddles a cut. See [Across a split](/recording/auto-zoom/#across-a-split). A planned zoom that meets an action already on the clip is dropped. `replace` removes only zooms, never any other action. A clip that already has a shutter keeps it.
159	
160	It answers as an edit does, and adds:
161	
162	| Key | What it holds |
163	| --- | --- |
164	| `visits` | How many visits were planned. |
165	| `added`, `replaced`, `dropped` | Zooms added, existing zooms removed, and planned zooms dropped because they met an action. |
166	| `closed_at_cut` | Visits closed at a cut, because the later half wasn't named in the call or has an action of its own there. |
167	| `bases_set` | Later halves whose base was set, by a zoom held across a cut or by `replace` putting it back. |
168	| `blurred` | How many clips were given `motion_blur`. |
169	| `actions` | A list of `{clip, at, duration, kind}`, with `at` in clip ticks and `kind` one of `in`, `pan`, `follow` or `back`. |
170	
171	Besides [the shared rules](#the-tools-that-work-from-a-cursor-file), it won't run when a number is out of range, a clip has no picture, or a clip is placed smaller than the canvas. For that last one, nest the clip, open the nest with `set_scope` and call `auto_zoom` inside it.
172	
173	## `add_shortcut_overlays`
174	
175	Places one Keyboard keys graphic clip for each keyboard shortcut recorded, at the moment it was pressed, as one undo step, **Add Shortcut Overlays**. It's **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays**, which has no sheet, so an agent is the only way to choose these settings. See [Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/).
176	
177	Only shortcuts are recorded, never typed keys, and only when the recording was made with **Record shortcuts** or `keys: "shortcuts"`. See [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/).
178	
179	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
180	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
181	| `clip` | integer | One of these | A screen recording's media clip. |
182	| `clips` | array of integers | One of these | Media clips whose media have cursor files. |
183	| `duration` | number | No | How long each overlay shows, in seconds: 0.5 to 10. Default: 1.5. |
184	| `position` | string | No | Where the keycaps sit: `bottom` (the default), `center` or `top`. |
185	| `theme` | string | No | The keycaps' look: `dark` (the default) or `light`. |
186	| `from` | integer | No | Places only shortcuts at or after this time, in ticks. |
187	| `to` | integer | No | Places only shortcuts before this time, in ticks. |
188	
189	An overlay never lasts less than 10 frames for each keycap plus 25, the time the template needs to press its last key and exit. Overlays never overlap:
190	
191	- The same shortcut pressed again before its overlay ends extends it, labelled ×2, ×3 and so on.
192	- A different shortcut pressed sooner ends the earlier overlay where it starts, once the earlier one has had its minimum. If that puts it more than 0.5 seconds after its press, it's dropped.
193	
194	The clips go on the front-most track named **Shortcuts** when it's in front of every clip's track, unlocked, shown, not a matte and free over their span. Otherwise they go on a new **Shortcuts** track at the front. A module in `graphics/` whose text equals the bundled template is reused, and otherwise the template is copied in once, only when something is placed.
195	
196	The overlays are ordinary graphic clips. See [Change an overlay](/recording/shortcut-overlays/#change-an-overlay).
197	
198	It answers as an edit does, and adds:
199	
200	| Key | What it holds |
201	| --- | --- |
202	| `added`, `merged`, `dropped` | Overlays placed, repeat presses folded into one, and presses left out. |
203	| `track`, `new_track` | The track used, and whether it's new. |
204	| `module`, `written` | The module drawn, and whether the template was copied in. |
205	| `overlays` | A list of `{at, duration, keys, label}`, with `at` in timeline ticks. |
206	
207	Besides [the shared rules](#the-tools-that-work-from-a-cursor-file), it won't run with a `duration`, `position` or `theme` out of range.
208	
209	## `speed_up_typing`
210	
211	Plays the typing in screen recordings faster, keeping speech and shortcuts at normal speed, as one undo step, **Speed Up Typing**. It's **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…**. See [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/).
212	
213	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
214	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
215	| `clip` | integer | One of these | A screen recording's media clip. |
216	| `clips` | array of integers | One of these | Media clips whose media have cursor files. Halves of a split recording are joined. |
217	| `rate` | number | No | How much faster a stretch plays: 2 to 8. Default: 4. |
218	| `shortest` | number | No | The shortest stretch sped up, in seconds: 1 to 30. Default: 3. |
219	| `keep_pitch` | boolean | No | Keeps the sped sound's pitch. Default: true. |
220	| `from` | integer | No | Speeds only typing at or after this time, in ticks. |
221	| `to` | integer | No | Speeds only typing before this time, in ticks. |
222	
223	A typing stretch is a run of at least 3 typed keys, each under 1 second apart. Taken out of each stretch are every span of speech, in any clip with sound under it on any track, and each recorded shortcut with its overlay, which is 1.5 seconds when it has no clip on a **Shortcuts** track. The pieces of all the clips join where they meet, and a piece shorter than `shortest` is left alone.
224	
225	Each kept piece is sped by `retime_range` at `rate` on every unlocked track, keeping 0.3 seconds at normal speed at each end, so everything after it moves up in step. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
226	
227	Speech detection runs on your Mac. A media with sound under a stretch that has no speech saved yet gets its spans in the same step.
228	
229	It answers `ok`, a `project` summary and the ids it created, and adds:
230	
231	| Key | What it holds |
232	| --- | --- |
233	| `stretches`, `short` | Stretches sped up, and pieces left alone for being too short. |
234	| `ranges` | A list of `{from, to, sped_to}`, in timeline ticks before the edit. |
235	| `saved` | The time saved, in ticks. |
236	| `speech_saved` | The media whose speech was saved in this step. |
237	| `audio_left_out`, `audio_note` | Only when a clip with sound now plays past ×12, the ceiling for sound. Unlike the menu command, it doesn't ask. See [If a clip would go silent](/recording/speed-up-typing/#if-a-clip-would-go-silent). |
238	
239	Besides [the shared rules](#the-tools-that-work-from-a-cursor-file), it won't run, and nothing changes, when:
240	
241	- `rate` or `shortest` is out of range.
242	- `retime_range` would refuse any range, because of a locked track after it, a transition or a linked clip, for example. The sentence names it.
243	- Speech detection is still running. It doesn't wait, and it says to try again in a moment.

7	
8	These tools turn the timeline into pictures and files. `render_frame` is how an agent sees what it has done, and `export`, `export_status` and `cancel_export` write the finished file.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['File ▸ Save Frame…', 'File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
12	  keys="⌘E"
13	  tools={['render_frame', 'export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
14	  needs="A client connected over MCP, or the Assistant tab."
15	/>
16	
17	Each tool has a heading here with its arguments. [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/) and [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/) walk through using them.
18	
19	Every tool here also takes `project`, the path of an open project. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/). None of them takes `scope`.

21	## `render_frame`
22	
23	Renders one frame of the finished timeline as a picture the model can see and a file on disk. It goes through the same composition and compositor an export does, so it shows what the file will hold at that moment. Use it before and after every edit. It's the same writer as **File ▸ Save Frame…**, so a PNG written here and one saved from the menu are byte-identical. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).
24	
25	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
26	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
27	| `t` | integer | No | The moment to render, in ticks, rounded to the frame grid. Default: the playhead. |
28	| `path` | string | No | Where to write the file. The folder must exist. Default: a temporary file. |
29	| `format` | string | No | `png`, `jpeg` or `heic`. Default: the path's own extension when it's one of those, else `png`. An explicit format wins, and the path's extension is replaced, so `shot.jpg` with `png` writes `shot.png`. |
30	| `max_width` | integer | No | Caps the image's width, 16 to 8192 pixels, aspect kept and never scaled up. Default: the canvas's own size. |
31	| `burn_in_timecode` | boolean | No | Draws the project timecode over the picture, topmost. Default: false. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
32	| `ungraded` | boolean | No | Draws as if no clip were graded, which is **View ▸ Show Ungraded**'s picture. Default: false. See [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/). |
33	| `sdr_version` | boolean | No | Draws an HDR project's SDR version, which is **View ▸ Show SDR Version**'s picture. An SDR project's frame doesn't change. Default: false. See [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/). |
34	| `selection` | integer | No | An adjustment clip's id. Draws what its qualifier selects, which is **View ▸ Show Selection**'s picture: grey, white fully graded and black untouched, with every layer in front of the clip left out. Black where the clip isn't on the frame. See [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/). |
35	| `waveform` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's luma waveform. Default: false. |
36	| `parade` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's RGB parade. Default: false. |
37	| `vectorscope` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's vectorscope. Default: false. |
38	| `vectorscope_zoom` | integer | No | The vectorscope's zoom: 1, 2 or 4. Needs `vectorscope: true`. Default: 1. |
39	| `histogram` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's histogram. Default: false. |
40	
41	The view switches themselves never reach this tool, so an agent asks for each picture here, whatever a person has switched on.
42	
43	It answers an image block and a text block. The text says the moment, the canvas's size and the size it rendered at, and its last sentence is "Written to `<path>`." Before that last sentence it can add:
44	
45	- A note that a JPEG flattened a transparent canvas onto black. PNG and HEIC keep the canvas's transparency.
46	- A graphic that warned or failed, naming it, its frame and the problem. A failed graphic draws its error card in the picture.
47	- A recorded cursor that couldn't be drawn: "The cursor of media M is not drawn:" and why. The clip draws without one.
48	- A clip with Remove Background whose masks weren't ready. It waits up to 30 seconds, then draws the clip uncut and names it.
49	- What each scope measured.
50	
51	**Scopes.** Each scope you ask for adds a sentence and writes a JSON file beside the image, named `<image path>.waveform.json`, `.parade.json`, `.vectorscope.json` or `.histogram.json`. The waveform and histogram sentences give the share of pixels clipping high and low, the parade gives it for each channel, and the vectorscope gives the share that's neutral. The waveform, parade and vectorscope count into 256 × 256 bins, and the histogram into 256 levels. At zoom 2 or 4, pixels off the vectorscope's plot aren't counted, and the text says what share they are. See [Scopes](/color/scopes/).
52	
53	**In an HDR project,** the frame is a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC labelled BT.2100 HLG. A JPEG, and any frame asked for with `sdr_version`, is the project's SDR version, labelled BT.709. Scopes read the picture drawn, so the HLG signal adds `signal: "hlg"` to each JSON file.
54	
55	**With a nest open,** it renders that nest, at its own canvas and from its own zero, which is what the preview is showing. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
56	
57	It won't render when:
58	
59	- `selection` isn't an adjustment clip of the project.
60	- `vectorscope_zoom` isn't 1, 2 or 4, or comes without `vectorscope: true`.
61	- `max_width` or `format` is out of range, `path` is empty, or the folder doesn't exist.
62	- There's no frame at that time, because it's past the end, the media is missing or the timeline is empty.
63	
64	## `export`
65	
66	Puts the timeline on the Export Queue and answers at once, as **File ▸ Export…** (<kbd>⌘E</kbd>) does with its sheet. It takes everything on the sheet but the frame rate: an export runs at the project's rate, or at 12.5 fps for `gif` and 25 fps for `apng`. An agent's export and a menu export go through the same exporter. See [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/).
67	
68	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
69	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
70	| `preset` | string | Yes | The encoding, one of the [presets](#the-presets). A wrong one is refused with the full list. |
71	| `path` | string | Yes | Where to write. The folder must exist. The format's extension is added when the path has none, and an existing file is replaced. |
72	| `size` | string or array of 2 integers | No | The sheet's **Size**: `document`, `2160p`, `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p`, `preset` (`gif` and `apng` only), or `[width, height]` in pixels, 16 to 8192 on each edge. Default: the document's size, or the format's cap on `gif` and `apng`. See [Export size](/export/size/). |
73	| `range` | string | No | `project` (the default) for the whole timeline, or `in_out` for the range `set_range` set. |
74	| `video_bitrate` | integer | No | Target video rate in bits per second, 1 or more, so 8000000 is 8 Mbps. Default: the preset decides. ProRes, `gif` and `apng` ignore it, and on AV1 and VP9 it's a soft cap. See [Export quality](/export/quality/). |
75	| `audio_bitrate` | integer | No | Target AAC or Opus rate in bits per second, 1 or more. Default: 192 kbps. ProRes, WAV and AIFF ignore it. |
76	| `audio_bits` | integer | No | `audio_wav`'s and `audio_aiff`'s bit depth, 16 or 24. Default: 16. Refused on every other preset. See [Export bit depth](/export/bit-depth/). |
77	| `loudness_lufs` | number | No | Normalises the whole mix to this integrated loudness, −70 to 0 LUFS. The sheet's rows are −14, −16 and −23. Omit it not to normalise. Ignored by `gif` and `apng`. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/). |
78	| `peak_dbtp` | number | No | The ceiling of the master limiter every export with sound runs, −20 to 0 dBTP. Default: −1. There's no off. |
79	| `burn_in_timecode` | boolean | No | Draws the project timecode over the picture. It shows project time even in a range export. Default: false. |
80	| `dynamic_range` | string | No | An HDR project's picture on `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422` and `prores_4444`: `hlg` (the default), `pq` for HDR10, or `sdr`. Every other video preset writes the SDR version. See [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/). |
81	| `encoder_speed` | string | No | `av1`'s and `av1_webm`'s speed: `faster`, `balanced` (the default) or `smaller`. Refused on every other preset. See [Encoder speed](/export/encoder-speed/). |
82	| `stems` | string | No | Also writes stems beside the mix on the three audio presets: `tracks` for one file per heard track, or `names` for one per track name. See [Audio stems](/export/stems/). |
83	
84	### The presets
85	
86	A preset is a container and a codec, with no size of its own, except that `gif` and `apng` each have a cap.
87	
88	| Preset | Writes | Good to know |
89	| --- | --- | --- |
90	| `h264` | H.264 in MP4 | 8-bit. What the export sheet opens on. |
91	| `hevc` | HEVC in MP4 | 8-bit. |
92	| `hevc_alpha` | HEVC with alpha in MOV | 8-bit. Keeps a transparent canvas. Safari's transparent movie. |
93	| `hevc_10bit` | HEVC in MP4 | 10-bit. |
94	| `av1` | AV1 in MP4 with AAC | 10-bit. Macs before M3 can't play it back. |
95	| `av1_webm` | AV1 in WebM with Opus | 10-bit. Macs before M3 can't play it back. |

107	
108	### What it answers
109	
110	`export` answers `{export_id, path, status}` at once, and `status` is `queued` or `running`. The job runs one at a time behind any other export already on the queue. An `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` or `vp9_alpha_webm` job also waits while the app's other AV1 and VP9 exports would hold more than a quarter of this Mac's memory with it, and a later job may run first meanwhile. The queue window isn't opened. The export always writes the whole document, even with a nest open.
111	
112	Follow it with [`export_status`](#export_status) and stop it with [`cancel_export`](#cancel_export). The `export_id` lasts until Frame Job quits.
113	
114	### When it refuses
115	
116	Every refusal comes back from this call, before anything is queued. `export` won't start when:
117	
118	- There's nothing on the timeline.
119	- `range` is `in_out` and the project has no in and out range.
120	- `preset` is unknown, or `size` isn't a row or a pair of edges from 16 to 8192. Each sentence lists what it takes.
121	- `size` is `preset` on anything but `gif` or `apng`.
122	- `audio_bits` or `encoder_speed` is on a preset that doesn't take it.
123	- `dynamic_range` is `hlg` or `pq` on a video preset that can't write it, or on any video preset in an SDR project, where `sdr` changes nothing. An audio preset ignores it.
124	- `stems` is on a movie preset, or no track can be heard.
125	- The folder doesn't exist.
126	- A graphic clip's module doesn't compile.
127	
128	A failure while writing comes back from `export_status` instead. That includes a `[width, height]` more than a pixel off the canvas's shape on `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha` or `vp9_alpha_webm`, because padding would destroy the alpha those presets are chosen for. It also includes a graphic that fails during the export, which stops it with no file left and names the graphic and the frame, and a stem whose file would replace media the project uses.
129	
130	## `export_status`
131	
132	Answers how an export is going. It's the job's row in **Window ▸ Export Queue**, read now. It never waits, so call it again after a pause until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
133	
134	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
135	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
136	| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` answered, 1 or more. |
137	
138	Every answer has `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed`, the seconds since `export` was called, or up to the finish once it has finished. The rest depends on `status`:
139	
140	| Status | Adds |
141	| --- | --- |
142	| `queued` | `waiting`, the queue row's sentence, while the job waits for memory behind other AV1 and VP9 exports. |
143	| `queued` or `running` | `estimated_seconds` on `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`: the export sheet's estimate of the whole write, in whole seconds. |
144	| `running` | `progress`, 0 to 1, and `phase` while the exporter names one, such as the loudness measurement. |
145	| `done` | What the file holds, below. |
146	| `failed`, `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
147	
148	When it's `done`, it adds:
149	
150	| Key | What it holds |
151	| --- | --- |
152	| `ok`, `bytes` | True, and the file's size. |
153	| `preset`, `container`, `codec`, `width`, `height`, `fps`, `start`, `duration` | The settings used. `fps` is `[num, den]`, and the width and height are the file's. |
154	| `burn_in_timecode` | Whether the burn-in was asked for. |
155	| `dynamic_range` | In an HDR project, the picture written. |
156	| `encoder_speed` | On `av1` and `av1_webm`. |
157	| `audio_bits` | On `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. |
158	| `stems` | With `stems`, a list of `{name, tracks, path}`, one for each file beside the mix. |
159	| `loudness` | For every format that carries sound, normalised or not: `summary`, `integrated_lufs`, `true_peak_dbtp`, `sample_peak_dbfs`, `gain_db`, `ceiling_dbtp`, `limited_db`, `capped_by_gain`, and `target_lufs` when one was asked for. Absent when there was no sound to measure. |
160	| `graphic_warnings` | A list of `{name, frame, message}`, each distinct warning a graphic gave while the file was drawn. Absent when there were none. |
161	| `cursor_warnings` | A list of `{media, path, message}`, each media whose cursor file couldn't be drawn, so its clips drew without one. Absent when there were none. |
162	
163	`integrated_lufs` is absent for a programme too short or too quiet to have one, and `summary` says so in words. `limited_db` says how far the limiter turned the hottest peak down, and `capped_by_gain` is true when the +40 dB gain cap decided the gain.
164	
165	Only ids `export` answered since Frame Job launched are known. Anything else is refused, and that includes a job a person put on the queue. A finished job's answer outlives its queue row, so it still reads after **Remove** or **Clear Finished**.
166	
167	## `cancel_export`
168	
169	Stops an export, as **Cancel** in its Export Queue row does. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
170	
171	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
172	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
173	| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` answered, 1 or more. |
174	
175	A queued export is cancelled before it starts. A running one stops and its half-written file is removed, though the answer may still read `running` until the writer has stopped, when `export_status` reads `cancelled`. A finished export is left alone.
176	
177	It answers as `export_status` does, and it refuses an id `export` didn't answer since launch.

description: "Render one frame of the finished timeline so an agent can see its work, choose the file it writes, draw grade and HDR variants, and measure the scopes."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

`render_frame` draws one frame of the finished timeline, so an agent can see what it has done. It goes through the same composition and compositor an export uses, so the picture is what the file will contain at that moment, not a preview of it.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Save Frame…"
  keys="⌥⌘E"
  tools="render_frame"
/>

## Render a frame

With no arguments it draws the frame under the playhead at the canvas's size and writes a PNG to a temporary file.

```json
{ "t": 1200000, "path": "/tmp/shot.png", "max_width": 960 }
```

The picture comes back two ways: as an image the model can see, and as a file on disk. The text beside it says what was drawn and ends by naming the file:

```
Frame at 1200000 ticks of a 1920×1080 px canvas, rendered at 960×540 px. Written to /tmp/shot.png.
```

It uses the same writer as [**File ▸ Save Frame…**](/export/save-frame/), so a PNG from either one is identical, byte for byte.

With a [nest](/mcp/nests/) open, it draws that nest at its own size, from its own zero, without the nest clip's position, scale or opacity. It takes no `scope`, so open the nest with `set_scope` to look inside.

| [`format`](#format) | string | No | `png`, `jpeg` or `heic`. | From the path, else `png` |
| [`max_width`](#max_width) | integer | No | Caps the width in pixels, 16 to 8192. | The canvas's width |

20	## Render a frame
21	
22	With no arguments it draws the frame under the playhead at the canvas's size and writes a PNG to a temporary file.
23	
24	```json
25	{ "t": 1200000, "path": "/tmp/shot.png", "max_width": 960 }

27	
28	The picture comes back two ways: as an image the model can see, and as a file on disk. The text beside it says what was drawn and ends by naming the file:
29	
30	```
31	Frame at 1200000 ticks of a 1920×1080 px canvas, rendered at 960×540 px. Written to /tmp/shot.png.
32	```
33	
34	It uses the same writer as [**File ▸ Save Frame…**](/export/save-frame/), so a PNG from either one is identical, byte for byte.

39	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
40	| [`t`](#t) | integer | No | The moment to render, in ticks. | The playhead |

42	| [`format`](#format) | string | No | `png`, `jpeg` or `heic`. | From the path, else `png` |

46	| [`selection`](#selection) | integer | No | Draws what an adjustment clip's qualifier selects. | None |
47	| [`sdr_version`](#sdr_version) | boolean | No | Draws an HDR project's SDR version. | `false` |
