54	
55	## Choose the moment and the file
56	
57	### `t`
58	
59	The moment to render, in ticks, 600,000 to the second. It's rounded to the project's frame grid. Leave it out for the playhead. A time before zero draws the first frame, and a time past the end is refused.
60	
61	With a nest open, `t` and the playhead are the nest's own time.
62	
63	### `path`
64	
65	Where to write the file, for example `~/Desktop/shot.png`. The folder must already exist, because Frame Job won't create one. An empty `path` is refused.
66	
67	Leave it out for a temporary file. Either way, the last sentence of the text names the file written.
68	
69	### `format`
70	
71	The kind of file to write.
72	
73	| `format` | What you get |
74	| --- | --- |
75	| `png` | Lossless, keeping the canvas's transparency. |
76	| `jpeg` | Quality 0.9. JPEG has no transparency, so a transparent canvas is flattened onto black, and the text always says so. |
77	| `heic` | Quality 0.9, keeping the canvas's transparency. |
78	
79	With no `format`, the path's extension decides: `.jpg` and `.jpeg` both mean JPEG, and `.heic` means HEIC. Any other path writes a PNG.
80	
81	An explicit `format` wins, and the path's extension is replaced rather than added to, so `{"path": "shot.jpg", "format": "png"}` writes `shot.png`. Only an extension Frame Job knows is replaced: `Talk v1.2` becomes `Talk v1.2.png`, not `Talk v1.png`. A JPEG always ends `.jpg`, so `shot.jpeg` is written as `shot.jpg`.
82	
83	`jpg` also works as a `format`, and capitals don't matter.
84	
85	### `max_width`
86	
87	Caps the image's width in pixels, from 16 to 8192. The picture keeps its shape and is never made larger than the canvas. Leave it out for the canvas's own size.
88	
89	A smaller frame is quicker to send and to look at. The [scopes](#measure-the-frame) measure the frame as written, so their counts cover fewer pixels too.
90	
91	## Change what's drawn
92	
93	These four draw something other than the plain picture. The view switches in the window never reach this tool or an export, so an agent asks here.
94	
95	### `burn_in_timecode`
96	
97	Draws the project timecode over the picture, on top of everything, as the export sheet's **Burn in timecode** does. It's the project's own timecode, in the toolbar's spelling. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/).
98	
99	### `ungraded`
100	
101	Draws every clip as if it weren't graded: Light, Color, wheels and curves neutral, and no look. It's the picture **View ▸ Show Ungraded** gives. See [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/).
102	
103	### `selection`
104	
105	Takes an adjustment clip's id and draws what its qualifier selects, in place of grading. It's the picture **View ▸ Show Selection** gives.
106	
107	- White is fully graded, and black is untouched.
108	- It's the blurred selection when the qualifier has a blur, and it's multiplied by any matte cutting the clip.
109	- The clip's strength isn't applied.
110	- Every layer in front of the clip is left out.
111	- Where the clip isn't on the frame, the picture is black.
112	
113	Frame Job won't do this for any other kind of clip. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).
114	
115	### `sdr_version`
116	
117	Draws an [HDR project's](/hdr/dynamic-range/) SDR version, the picture **View ▸ Show SDR Version** gives. White titles come back near white, and highlights above reference white roll off. It's what the SDR exports and JPEG frames hold.
118	
119	In an SDR project it changes nothing, and the frame comes out identical. See [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/).
120	
121	## Measure the frame
122	
123	Each scope argument measures the rendered frame through the same analyser as the [**View ▸ Scopes**](/color/scopes/) panel, so the two can't count differently. The text gives the headline figures, and a JSON file beside the image holds the counts, named after it: `shot.png` gets `shot.png.waveform.json`.
124	
125	The scopes read the frame as it was drawn, so `max_width`, `burn_in_timecode`, `ungraded` and `selection` all change what they count.
126	
127	If the measurement can't run, the call comes back as an error, but the image is already written and the error names it: "Wrote …, but its waveform could not be measured: the GPU pass did not run."
128	
129	### `waveform`, `parade` and `histogram`
130	
131	- **`waveform`** measures luma. The text gives the share of pixels clipping high and low.
132	- **`parade`** measures R′, G′ and B′ the way the waveform measures luma. The text gives the share clipping high and low for each channel.
133	- **`histogram`** counts R′, G′, B′ and Y′ at 256 levels. The text gives the share clipping high and low, read from Y′.
134	
135	For example: "Waveform: highlights clipped in 0.4 % of pixels, shadows in 0.0 %; its 256 × 256 counts are in …". A pixel clips high at level 255 and low at level 0.
136	
137	| JSON key | `waveform` | `parade` | `histogram` |
138	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
139	| `width`, `height` | The frame measured | The frame measured | The frame measured |
140	| `levels` | 256 | 256 | 256 |
141	| `columns` | 256 | 256 | |
142	| `counts` | 256 column bins, each 256 levels | The same, under `red`, `green` and `blue` | |
143	| `red`, `green`, `blue`, `luma` | | | 256 counts each |
144	| `clipped_high`, `clipped_low` | Pixels clipping | Pixels clipping, by channel | Pixels clipping, by Y′ |
145	| `marks_high`, `marks_low` | The column bins where at least 0.5 % of the column clips | The same, by channel | |
146	| `highlights`, `shadows` | Percentages | | Percentages |
147	
148	### `vectorscope` and `vectorscope_zoom`
149	
150	`vectorscope` measures Rec. 709 Cb and Cr of the encoded values in 256 × 256 bins centred on neutral, bin 128. The text gives the share of pixels that are neutral.
151	
152	`vectorscope_zoom` is 1, 2 or 4, like the 1×, 2× and 4× cells on a [vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) slot, and it needs `vectorscope: true`. Zooming spreads a near-grey picture over more bins. At 2 and 4, a pixel off the plot isn't counted, and the text also gives the share that lie off it.
153	
154	| JSON key | What it holds |
155	| --- | --- |
156	| `width`, `height` | The frame measured. |
157	| `bins`, `centre` | 256 and 128. |
158	| `matrix`, `values` | `Rec. 709` and `encoded`. |
159	| `counts` | 256 arrays by Cr bin, each indexed by Cb bin. |
160	| `neutral` | Pixels in the neutral bin. |
161	| `zoom` | The zoom. |
162	| `off_plot` | Pixels left off the plot. Always 0 at 1. |
163	| `targets` | The six 75 % colour targets, `R`, `Mg`, `B`, `Cy`, `G` and `Yl`, each `[cb, cr]` in bins at this zoom, or `null` off the plot. |
164	| `skin_line_degrees` | The skin line's angle. |
165	
166	## Read what the answer says
167	
168	The text always starts with the frame's time and sizes and ends with "Written to …". Anything else worth saying sits between the two.
169	
170	### Graphic problems in the answer
171	
172	When a [graphic](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/) in the frame had a problem, the answer names it with its frame and the diagnostic:
173	
174	- `Graphic "lower-third" failed at frame 12: …`
175	- `Graphic "lower-third" warned at frame 12: …`
176	- `Graphic "lower-third" does not compile: …`
177	
178	A failed graphic draws its error card in the picture.
179	
180	### Waiting for cutout masks
181	
182	A clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) waits up to 30 s for the masks the frame needs. Frame Job starts making them as soon as the cutout is set, on your Mac.
183	
184	Past 30 s the clip is drawn whole, and the answer says so: "Clip 12 is drawn uncut: its person masks were not ready within 30 s." For a picture with its subject set to foreground, it says "its foreground masks".
185	
186	So after setting a cutout, read that sentence before trusting the frame. [`analyze_cutout`](/mcp/tools-analysis/) can wait for the masks first.
187	
188	### A cursor that can't be drawn
189	
190	A screen recording's cursor is drawn from its cursor file. When the file can't be read, the clip draws without one and the answer says "The cursor of media 5 is not drawn: …".
191	
192	## Frames from an HDR project
193	
194	In an [HLG project](/hdr/dynamic-range/), the frame depends on the format:
195	
196	| What you ask for | What you get |
197	| --- | --- |
198	| `png` | 16-bit, labelled BT.2100 HLG |
199	| `heic` | 10-bit, labelled BT.2100 HLG |
200	| `jpeg` | The project's SDR version, labelled BT.709 |
201	| Any format with `sdr_version` | The project's SDR version, labelled BT.709 |
202	
203	Scopes read the picture drawn. On the HLG picture they read the HLG signal, and on the SDR version they read as an SDR project's do.
204	
205	On the HLG signal:
206	
207	- Each scope's JSON adds `signal: "hlg"`.
208	- The waveform, parade and histogram JSON add `scale`: `unit` (`cd/m²`), `ticks` (each with `percent`, `level` and `nits`), `reference_white_percent` (75) and `clip_percent` (100).
209	- Luma takes Rec. 2020's weights, and the vectorscope takes Rec. 2020's matrix and targets.
210	- The text says so. The waveform's reads "reference white at 75 %, 203 cd/m², and 100 % at 1,000 cd/m²".
211	
212	See [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/) and [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/).
213	
214	## When it won't render
215	
216	Nothing is drawn in these cases, and the answer says why.
217	
218	| It says | What to do |
219	| --- | --- |
220	| "No frame at … Either the time is past the end of the timeline, the media is missing, or the timeline is empty." | Check `duration` and `missing_media` in [`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/). |
221	| "There is no folder at … to write into." | Create the folder, or choose another `path`. |
222	| "path must name a file to write — omit it for a temporary one." | The `path` was empty. |
223	| "format must be one of png, jpeg, heic (got …)." | Use one of the three. |
224	| "max_width must be 16…8192 px (got …)." | Use a width in range. |
225	| "selection must name an adjustment clip of this project; clip … is not one." | Pass an adjustment clip's id. An adjustment clip can't be inside a nest, so close any open nest first. |
226	| "vectorscope_zoom must be 1, 2 or 4 (got …)." | Use one of the three. |
227	| "vectorscope_zoom needs vectorscope: true." | Add `vectorscope: true`. |

236	title: "Export: start, then poll"
237	description: Write a file from an agent, follow the job until it finishes, stop it, and read what the file holds.
238	---
239	
240	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
241	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
242	
243	Use these three tools to write the timeline to a file from an agent, follow the job and stop it. `export` doesn't wait for the file. It checks the request, puts a job on the Export Queue and returns at once, and the agent then asks how the job is going until it ends.
244	
245	<AtAGlance
246	  menu={['File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
247	  keys="⌘E"
248	  where="The export sheet's Add to Queue, and each row's Cancel in the Export Queue"
249	  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
250	/>
251	
252	## Write a file
253	
254	<Steps>
255	
256	1. Call `export` with a preset and a path. It returns straight away.
257	
258	   ```json
259	   { "preset": "h264", "path": "/Volumes/Edits/cut", "size": "1080p" }
260	   ```
261	
262	   ```json
263	   { "export_id": 3, "path": "/Volumes/Edits/cut.mp4", "status": "running" }
264	   ```
265	
266	2. Call `export_status` with that `export_id`, pause, and call it again until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
267	
268	3. Read the `done` result. It says what the file holds, including the loudness it measured and any warnings.
269	
270	</Steps>
271	
272	To stop the job, call `cancel_export`. The job shows in **Window ▸ Export Queue** like any other, but the window doesn't open by itself.
273	
274	## Export
275	
276	`export` does what **File ▸ Export…** does with **Add to Queue**, and it writes the file the same way, so an agent's file and a person's match. It takes the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)'s controls in the sheet's own terms, apart from the frame rate.
277	
278	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
279	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
280	| `preset` | string | Yes | The encoding: a container and a codec. See [Presets](#presets). |
281	| `path` | string | Yes | Where to write, such as `~/Movies/cut.mp4`. See [Path handling](#path-handling). |
282	| `size` | string or `[width, height]` | No | The output size. See [Size](#size). |
283	| `range` | string | No | `project` for the whole timeline, or `in_out` for the in and out range. See [Range](#range). |
284	| `video_bitrate` | integer | No | Target video rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
285	| `audio_bitrate` | integer | No | Target AAC or Opus rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
286	| `loudness_lufs` | number | No | Normalise the whole mix to this loudness, −70 to 0. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
287	| `peak_dbtp` | number | No | The master limiter's ceiling, −20 to 0. See [Peak dBTP](#peak-dbtp). |
288	| `audio_bits` | integer | No | 16 or 24, for WAV and AIFF. See [Audio bits](#audio-bits). |
289	| `stems` | string | No | `tracks` or `names`, to write stems beside an audio mix. See [Stems](#stems). |
290	| `burn_in_timecode` | boolean | No | Draw the project timecode over the picture, on top of everything. Off by default. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
291	| `dynamic_range` | string | No | `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`, in an HLG project. See [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range). |
292	| `encoder_speed` | string | No | `faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`, for AV1. See [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
293	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to export, as `get_project` reports it. Without it, the frontmost project. |
294	
295	It returns `{export_id, path, status}`. `path` is the file that will be written, with `~` expanded and the extension corrected. `status` is `running` if the job started at once, or `queued` if it's waiting.
296	
297	Jobs in the queue run one at a time, behind anything already there. A job writes the project as it stood when `export` was called, so later edits don't reach it. Calling `export` pauses playback in that project's window.
298	
299	`export` takes no `scope`. With a [nest](/mcp/nests/) open it still writes the project's timeline, not the nest's.
300	
301	## Export status
302	
303	`export_status` reports how a job is going, as its row in the Export Queue does, and it never waits. Pass the `export_id`, which is an integer of 1 or more.
304	
305	Every result carries `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed`, the seconds since `export` was called, or from then to the finish once the job has ended. The rest depends on the status.
306	
307	| `status` | Also carries |
308	| --- | --- |
309	| `queued` | `waiting` while an AV1 or VP9 job is held for memory. `estimated_seconds` on `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`. |
310	| `running` | `progress`, from 0 to 1. `phase` while the export names one, which is "Measuring loudness…" during the first pass over the mix. `estimated_seconds` on the same four presets. |
311	| `done` | What the file holds, in the next table. |
312	| `failed` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
313	| `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
314	
315	`estimated_seconds` is the export sheet's estimate of the whole export in whole seconds, and it's only an estimate.
316	
317	`waiting` is a sentence such as "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.1 GB of the 8.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 7.0 GB." AV1 and VP9 exports may hold a quarter of this Mac's memory between them, though a job with no other running always starts. While one is held, a later job in the queue may run first.
318	
319	A `done` result adds these keys.
320	
321	| Key | What it holds |
322	| --- | --- |
323	| `ok` | `true`. |
324	| `bytes` | The file's size. |
325	| `preset`, `container`, `codec` | What was written. |
326	| `width`, `height` | The file's size in pixels. These are reported on audio presets too, where they mean nothing. |
327	| `fps` | The rate as `[num, den]`, such as `[30, 1]`. |
328	| `start`, `duration` | The part of the timeline written, in [ticks](/mcp/units-and-ids/). |
329	| `burn_in_timecode` | Whether the argument was on. |
330	| `dynamic_range` | The picture written: `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`. Only for a video preset in an HLG project. |
331	| `encoder_speed` | The speed used. Only on `av1` and `av1_webm`. |
332	| `audio_bits` | The depth written. Only on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. |
333	| `stems` | `[{name, tracks, path}]`, one per file beside the mix. Only when `stems` was asked for. |
334	| `loudness` | What the mix measured. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
335	| `graphic_warnings` | `[{name, frame, message}]`, each distinct warning a graphic gave while the file was drawn. Collecting stops after 64 distinct reports, so a noisy graphic's list can be cut short. `frame` is the graphic's own frame, or `null`. Absent when there were none. |
336	| `cursor_warnings` | `[{media, path, message}]`, each media whose cursor file couldn't be drawn. Its clips were written without a cursor. Absent when there were none. |
337	
338	## Cancel export
339	
340	`cancel_export` stops a job, as the row's **Cancel** does, and returns what `export_status` would. Pass the `export_id`.
341	
342	| The job is | What happens |
343	| --- | --- |
344	| Queued | It's cancelled before it starts. The result reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled before it started." |
345	| Running | It stops and its half-written file is removed. The result may still read `running` until writing has stopped, and `export_status` then reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled." |
346	| Finished | It's left alone, and its file stays. The result is the finished job's. |
347	
348	## Export id and its lifetime
349	
350	An `export_id` is known until Frame Job quits. Removing a finished row from the Export Queue, or choosing **Clear Finished**, doesn't lose it, so an agent can still read how that job ended.
351	
352	An id belongs to the launch, not to a project, so `export_status` and `cancel_export` don't need `project`. Only ids that `export` returned are known. A job a person queued from the sheet has no id an agent can follow. Any other number returns the error "No export this launch has export_id 7 — ids come from export and last until Frame Job quits."
353	
354	## Refusals and failures
355	
356	A problem Frame Job can see from the request comes back from `export` itself as an error, and nothing is queued.
357	
358	| The request | What stops it |
359	| --- | --- |
360	| An empty timeline | "There is nothing on the timeline to export." |
361	| A folder that doesn't exist | "There is no folder at … to write into." Frame Job never creates the folder. |
362	| An unknown preset | The error lists all the presets. |
363	| An unknown `size`, or one it can't read | The error lists the sizes. See [Size](#size). |
364	| `range` of `in_out` with no range set | "This project has no in/out range — set one with set_range `{start, end}`, or export with range \"project\"." |
365	| A number out of range, or a word it doesn't know | The error names the argument and the value. |
366	| An option the preset doesn't have | See [Audio bits](#audio-bits), [Stems](#stems), [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range) and [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
367	| A graphic clip in the range with no module, or a module that doesn't compile | "The export was not started: the graphic "…" does not compile — …. Fix the module and export again." A clip with no module reads "has no module in graphics/" in place of "does not compile — …". It names each graphic and its first error, and it covers graphics inside nests. An audio-only preset draws no graphics, so it isn't stopped by one. |
368	
369	Anything that goes wrong after that comes back from `export_status` as `failed`, with the sentence in `reason`. Check for it even when `export` answered cleanly.
370	
371	| What went wrong | The `reason` |
372	| --- | --- |
373	| A size of another shape on a transparent preset | "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…". See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets). |
374	| A stem's file would be one of the project's media | "The stem “…” would replace media this project uses; export under another name." |
375	| A graphic fails while it's drawn | "The export was stopped at frame … of the graphic "…": …. No file was written." |
376	| A retimed clip's sound, an isolated voice or a voice effect couldn't be rendered | The sentence names the clip and the reason. |
377	| A cut-out clip's masks couldn't be made | "Clip …'s person masks could not be made: …." A picture cut out by **Foreground** says foreground masks. |
378	| A clip's gate, leveller or de-esser needs a loudness that hasn't been measured | "Clip …'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…". Wait for the clip's analysis, then export again. |
379	| This Mac has no encoder for the preset | "This Mac cannot export with the “…” preset." |
380	
381	A graphic's warnings are different: they don't stop the export, and they arrive as `graphic_warnings` in the `done` result.
382	
383	## Presets
384	
385	There are 15 presets, one per encoding. A preset says nothing about size. These are the rows of the sheet's **Format** control, described in [Choose a format](/export/formats/). A wrong id's error lists them all.
386	
387	| Preset | In the sheet | File | Picture | Sound |
388	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
389	| `h264` | H.264 (MP4) | `.mp4` | 8-bit. The sheet's first row. | AAC |
390	| `hevc` | HEVC (MP4) | `.mp4` | 8-bit | AAC |
391	| `hevc_alpha` | HEVC with Alpha (MOV) | `.mov` | 8-bit with transparency. Safari's transparent movie. | AAC |
392	| `hevc_10bit` | HEVC 10-bit (MP4) | `.mp4` | 10-bit | AAC |
393	| `av1` | AV1 (MP4) | `.mp4` | 10-bit | AAC |
394	| `av1_webm` | AV1 (WebM) | `.webm` | 10-bit | Opus |
395	| `vp9_webm` | VP9 (WebM) | `.webm` | 8-bit (Profile 0) for an SDR picture, 10-bit (Profile 2) for HLG and PQ. One speed. | Opus |
396	| `vp9_alpha_webm` | VP9 with Alpha (WebM) | `.webm` | Always 8-bit, with transparency. The transparent movie Chrome and Firefox play. | Opus |
397	| `prores_422` | ProRes 422 (MOV) | `.mov` | 10-bit. An editing master. | 16-bit LPCM |
398	| `prores_4444` | ProRes 4444 (MOV) | `.mov` | 12-bit with transparency. A master. | 16-bit LPCM |
399	| `audio_m4a` | Audio only (M4A) | `.m4a` | None | AAC |
400	| `audio_wav` | Audio only (WAV) | `.wav` | None | 48 kHz LPCM, 16 or 24 bits |
401	| `audio_aiff` | Audio only (AIFF) | `.aiff` | None | 48 kHz LPCM, 16 or 24 bits |
402	| `gif` | Animated GIF | `.gif` | 256 colours. Fits inside 480 × 270 unless `size` says otherwise. | None |
403	| `apng` | Animated PNG | `.png` | Lossless, with transparency. Fits inside 960 × 540 unless `size` says otherwise. | None |
404	
405	Macs before M3 can't play `av1` and `av1_webm` back.
406	
407	## Frame rate
408	
409	There's no frame-rate argument, so the sheet's [frame rate](/export/frame-rate/) control has no agent equivalent. An export runs at the project's rate, `gif` at 12.5 fps and `apng` at 25 fps. The `done` result's `fps` says which, with 12.5 fps as `[25, 2]`.
410	
411	## Path handling
412	
413	The folder must exist. A `~` at the start is expanded, and an existing file at the path is replaced.
414	
415	The file always ends in the preset's extension.
416	
417	| `path` | `preset` | Writes | Why |
418	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
419	| `cut.mp4` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | The extension is already right. |
420	| `cut` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | With no extension, it's added. |
421	| `cut.mov` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | A different media extension is replaced. |
422	| `Talk v1.2` | `h264` | `Talk v1.2.mp4` | Any other suffix stays part of the name. |
423	| `cut.webm` | `h264` | `cut.webm.mp4` | `.webm` isn't one of the extensions Frame Job replaces. |
424	| `cut.mp4` | `av1_webm` | `cut.webm` | `.mp4` is. |
425	
426	The extensions it replaces are `.mov`, `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.m4a`, `.mp3`, `.wav`, `.aif`, `.aiff`, `.caf`, `.framejob`, `.srt`, `.vtt`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.heic` and `.gif`. The returned `path` is always the file that gets written.
427	
428	## Size
429	
430	`size` is the sheet's **Size** control. See [Export size](/export/size/) for what the sizes mean to a person.
431	
432	| `size` | In the sheet | What it writes |
433	| --- | --- | --- |
434	| `document` | Document size | The project's own size. The default on every movie preset. |
435	| `2160p` | 4K | A short edge of 2160 pixels. |
436	| `1440p` | 1440p | A short edge of 1440 pixels. |
437	| `1080p` | 1080p | A short edge of 1080 pixels. |
438	| `720p` | 720p | A short edge of 720 pixels. |
439	| `preset` | GIF default, APNG default | The format's cap. `gif` and `apng` only, where it's the default. |
440	| `[width, height]` | Custom… | Exactly this size, from 16 to 8192 pixels on each edge. |
441	
442	The number is always the short edge, and the long edge follows the project's shape, rounded to an even number. A vertical project's `1080p` is 1080 × 1920. Every size means the same on every project, so a 1920 × 1080 project's `1080p` is its own size, and a size larger than the project scales it up.
443	
444	A movie is written at exactly the size asked for. If the shape differs from the project's by more than a pixel, the picture is letterboxed. Within a pixel, it fills the frame instead.
445	
446	- **Even edges.** Every preset but `prores_4444`, `gif` and `apng` needs even dimensions, so an odd width or height is written one pixel smaller. That covers `document` on a project with an odd edge. The `done` result's `width` and `height` are the file's.
447	- **GIF and APNG.** A size is a box the picture is fitted inside, keeping its shape and never scaling up. A vertical 1080 × 1920 project's GIF default comes out at 152 × 270.
448	- **Audio presets.** A size has no effect, and `preset` isn't one of their sizes.
449	- **Transparent movies.** A `[width, height]` of another shape fails. See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets).
450	
451	An unknown size returns an error with the list, for example "No export size is called "480p" for h264. The sizes are: document, 2160p, 1440p, 1080p, 720p — or pass [width, height]." A custom size outside 16 to 8192 pixels is an error too. It isn't clamped.
452	
453	## Range
454	
455	`range` is the sheet's **Range** control. `project`, the default, writes the whole timeline. `in_out` writes the range set with `set_range`, and `export` returns an error when there's no range. See [Export a range](/export/range/).
456	
457	The range is snapped to the export's frame grid and kept inside the project. A range that comes to nothing is an error too.
458	
459	`burn_in_timecode` shows project time even in a range export, so a file written from 00:00:10:00 begins at 00:00 with a burn-in that reads 00:00:10:00.
460	
461	## Exact bitrates
462	
463	The sheet offers [quality](/export/quality/) tiers. An agent sets the rates directly, in bits per second, so 8 Mbps is `8000000`. Each must be a whole number from 1 to 4,294,967,295.
464	
465	`video_bitrate` is the target video rate. Without it, Frame Job works out a rate from the frame size and frame rate. ProRes, GIF and APNG ignore it, because ProRes is fixed by its profile and the other two have no bitrate.
466	
467	On the AV1 and VP9 presets it works differently:
468	
469	- **`av1` and `av1_webm`.** It's a soft cap. The encoder works at a constant quality matched to HEVC at that rate, and the file usually comes in well under it. Very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over. Without it, the quality is matched to HEVC at 0.07 bits per pixel per frame.
470	- **`vp9_webm`.** It's a soft cap too, matched to HEVC, or HEVC 10-bit in an HDR export. Up to about 1.15 times over was measured.
471	- **`vp9_alpha_webm`.** It's the same soft cap on the picture's stream alone. The transparency's stream comes on top, at a constant quality.
472	
473	`audio_bitrate` is the AAC or Opus rate, 192 kbps when absent. Opus takes the nearest rate its encoder offers. ProRes, WAV and AIFF ignore it, because they write LPCM.
474	
475	## The loudness report
476	
477	Every export with sound measures its own mix and reports it as `loudness` in the `done` result, normalised or not. GIF and APNG have no sound, and a timeline with no sound has nothing to measure, so `loudness` is absent from both.
478	
479	`loudness_lufs` normalises the whole mix to an integrated loudness, from −70 to 0. The sheet's [Loudness](/export/loudness/) rows are −14 for streaming, −16 for podcasts and −23 for EBU R 128 broadcast, and an agent can ask for any value, such as −14.5. The export measures itself first, then applies one gain to everything, through the master limiter. The file lands on the target with its loudest peaks limited, rather than the whole mix held down. GIF and APNG ignore it.
480	
481	| Key | What it holds |
482	| --- | --- |
483	| `summary` | The same line the queue row and the progress sheet show, such as "Peak −1.0 dBTP · −16.0 LUFS", with " · peaks limited by 8.6 dB" when the limiter took 0.05 dB or more. |
484	| `integrated_lufs` | The file's integrated loudness. Absent when it has none, and `summary` then says "loudness not measurable". |
485	| `true_peak_dbtp` | The file's true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
486	| `sample_peak_dbfs` | The file's sample peak, never above the true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
487	| `gain_db` | The gain applied to reach the target. |
488	| `ceiling_dbtp` | The master limiter's ceiling. |
489	| `limited_db` | How far the limiter turned the loudest peak down. |
490	| `capped_by_gain` | `true` when the +40 dB limit on the gain decided it, so the file may be short of the target. |
491	| `target_lufs` | The `loudness_lufs` asked for. Absent when none was. |
492	
493	A programme shorter than one 400 ms measuring block, or one too quiet to pass the standard's gate, has a peak and no integrated loudness. Digital silence reads "Silent" in `summary`.
494	
495	## Peak dBTP
496	
497	Every export with sound goes through a master limiter, so the file's true peak stays at or under a ceiling. `peak_dbtp` sets that ceiling, from −20 to 0. It's −1 when absent, which is the sheet's fixed value. 0 is the loosest, and there's no way to turn the limiter off.
498	
499	You can pass it with or without `loudness_lufs`. `limited_db` in the [report](#the-loudness-report) says how far the limiter turned the loudest peak down.
500	
501	## Audio bits
502	
503	`audio_bits` is the sheet's [Bit depth](/export/bit-depth/) control: 16, the default, or 24. It's rounded once from the mix and never dithered, and the `done` result repeats it.
504	
505	It works on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` only. On any other preset `export` returns the error "h264 has no bit depth; audio_bits applies to audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset. ProRes keeps 16-bit sound. Any other number is an error, whatever the preset.
506	
507	## Stems
508	
509	`stems` also writes [stems](/export/stems/) beside the mix, on `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. It's the sheet's **Stems** control.
510	
511	| `stems` | What it writes |
512	| --- | --- |
513	| `tracks` | One file per heard track. |
514	| `names` | One file per track name. Heard tracks whose names match, ignoring case, share a file, and an unnamed track gets its own. |
515	
516	A track is heard when it has sound in it and isn't muted or silenced by another track's solo. Each stem is named `<file> - <track name>.<ext>`, beside the mix, so `mix.wav` and a track called Voice give `mix - Voice.wav`. An unnamed track is `Track N`, and [Stem file names](/export/stems/#stem-file-names) has the other cases.
517	
518	A stem holds its tracks' sound before the master, with no loudness gain and no limiter, so the stems add up to the mix wherever the master changed nothing. Any file already at a stem's name is replaced.
519	
520	The `done` result lists each one as `stems [{name, tracks, path}]`. `tracks` holds the ids of the timeline tracks in that stem.
521	
522	- On any other preset `export` returns the error "h264 has no stems; stems applies to audio_m4a, audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset.
523	- With no track heard, the error is "stems: no track is heard, so there is no stem to write".
524	- If a stem's file would be one of the project's media, the job fails before any stem is written, and `export_status` gives the reason.
525	- A failed or cancelled job leaves neither the mix nor any stem behind.
526	
527	## Dynamic range
528	
529	`dynamic_range` chooses the picture an [HLG project](/hdr/dynamic-range/) writes. It's the sheet's **Dynamic Range** control.
530	
531	| `dynamic_range` | What it writes |
532	| --- | --- |
533	| `hlg` | BT.2100 HLG, with no Dolby Vision. The default on the presets that carry HDR. |
534	| `pq` | HDR10: BT.2100 PQ at 1,000 cd/m², with a P3-D65 mastering display of 0.005–1,000 cd/m², MaxCLL 1,000 and MaxFALL 0. |
535	| `sdr` | The project's SDR version. |
536	
537	The presets that carry HDR are `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422` and `prores_4444`. Every other video preset in an HLG project writes the SDR version, `vp9_alpha_webm` included, and audio presets ignore the argument.
538	
539	- `hlg` or `pq` on another video preset returns the error "h264 is 8-bit and writes the SDR version; export dynamic_range "pq" as hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, prores_422 or prores_4444".
540	- `hlg` or `pq` in an SDR project returns the error "dynamic_range "pq" needs an HLG project; set_canvas output "hlg" first".
541	- `sdr` in an SDR project changes nothing.
542	
543	Once a job is `done`, `dynamic_range` in the result names the picture that was written. An SDR project's result has no such key.
544	
545	## Encoder speed
546	
547	`encoder_speed` trades export time for file size on `av1` and `av1_webm`. It's the sheet's [Speed](/export/encoder-speed/) control, and the `done` result names the one used.
548	
549	| `encoder_speed` | SVT-AV1 preset | What it does |
550	| --- | --- | --- |
551	| `faster` | 8 | The quickest. |
552	| `balanced` | 6 | The default. |
553	| `smaller` | 4 | The smallest file for the picture, and the slowest. |
554	
555	On every other preset `export` returns the error "h264 has no encoder speed; encoder_speed applies to av1 and av1_webm", naming the preset. That includes `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`, which have one speed.
556	
557	## Transparent presets
558	
559	Four presets keep a transparent canvas transparent: `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha`, `vp9_alpha_webm` and `apng`. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). A GIF can show a fully transparent pixel, but it has no alpha channel, so nothing partial survives.
560	
561	On the three movie presets, a `[width, height]` of a different shape from the canvas can't be written, because the padding would destroy the alpha channel. `export` queues the job, and `export_status` then reads `failed` with a reason that names both sizes. The shape is judged after an odd edge is evened, and within a pixel the picture fills the frame, so a size in the canvas's own proportions always works, at any scale. Every named size already has the canvas's shape.
562	
563	`apng` fits its picture inside the size instead, so this doesn't apply to it.

586	    'Screen Recording permission, for a screen recording',
587	    'Microphone, Camera or Input Monitoring, only when the call uses them',
588	    'A person has to give each permission first',
589	  ]}
590	/>
591	
592	## Record the screen
593	
594	The smallest call names only `seconds`:
595	
596	```json
597	{ "seconds": 30 }
598	```
599	
600	That records the main display for 30 seconds with its system sound, leaves Frame Job's own windows out of the picture, and lands the movie at the playhead of the front project. A recording then goes through these stages:
601	
602	- **It starts at once.** There's no countdown and no panel.
603	- **It writes to disk.** The file goes to `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`, named for example `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov`, and it's never stored inside the project. A name that's already taken gets ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on.
604	- **It lands.** The movie becomes ordinary media, and a clip goes at the playhead on the front track of whatever is open, a [nest](/mcp/nests/) included. When that track has no room there, Frame Job adds a new track in front of everything. This is one undo step, **Add Recording**.
605	- **It answers.** The call returns once the recording is finished, imported and placed. See [What it answers](#what-it-answers).
606	
607	With no project open, the recording opens as a new untitled project instead, and `landed` reads `new_project`. Its canvas takes the movie's size and `rate`. Later calls address that project with `project` set to the recording's path, which is the path `get_project` reports for it. If the target project closes while the recording runs, the same thing happens and the note says so.
608	
609	Only one recording runs at a time, whoever started it. A second one is refused with "A recording is already in progress."
610	
611	:::note
612	The built-in [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) can't call `record_screen`. Recording stays with a person at the Record button, or an agent connected from outside.
613	:::
614	
615	[Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) has the landing in full, and it's the same for both.
616	
617	## Choose a source
618	
619	`source` says what's recorded.
620	
621	| `source` | What it records | Files |
622	| --- | --- | --- |
623	| `screen` | A display or a window. The default. | `Screen Recording <date> at <time>.mov` |
624	| `voice_over` | The default microphone alone, with no picture. | `Voice-over <date> at <time>.m4a` |
625	| `camera` | A camera alone, with no screen. | `Camera Recording <date> at <time>.mov` |
626	
627	An argument the source can't use is refused by name, not ignored. A JSON null counts as not given. This is what each source takes:
628	
629	| Argument | `screen` | `voice_over` | `camera` |
630	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
631	| `seconds`, `project`, `path`, `place`, `enhance` | Yes | Yes | Yes |
632	| `microphone` | Yes | Implied, and `false` is refused | Yes |
633	| `rate` | Yes | Yes, for a new project's canvas | Refused |
634	| `camera`, `camera_format` | Yes, [beside the screen](#record-a-camera-beside-the-screen) | Refused | Yes |
635	| `camera_layout`, `camera_cutout` | Yes, with `camera` | Refused | Refused |
636	| `display`, `window`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows` | Yes | Refused | Refused |
637	| `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `cursor`, `keys` | Yes | Refused | Refused |
638	| `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing` | Yes | Refused | Refused |
639	
640	## The arguments
641	
642	Only `seconds` is required. The sections further down cover the arguments for [voice-overs](#record-a-voice-over), [cameras](#record-a-camera-alone) and the [steps after landing](#run-steps-after-it-lands).

674	title: "Tools: speed and time"
675	description: "The agent tools that change a clip's speed, ramp it, retime a stretch of the timeline, play a clip backwards and hold a frame, with their arguments, answers and limits."
676	---
677	
678	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
679	
680	These tools change how time passes in a clip: its rate, a ramp between rates, a whole stretch of the timeline played faster or slower, the direction it plays, and a held frame.
681	
682	<AtAGlance tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'add_speed_ramp', 'retime_range', 'set_reversed', 'freeze_frame']} />
683	
684	## Pick a tool
685	
686	| You want to | Use |
687	| --- | --- |
688	| Play one clip at a rate, or fit it to a length | [`set_speed`](#set_speed) |
689	| Make a clip end at a time by changing its speed | [`rate_stretch`](#rate_stretch) |
690	| Ease a clip from one rate to another | [`add_speed_ramp`](#add_speed_ramp) |
691	| Play a stretch of the whole timeline faster or slower | [`retime_range`](#retime_range) |
692	| Play a clip backwards | [`set_reversed`](#set_reversed) |
693	| Hold one frame | [`freeze_frame`](#freeze_frame) |
694	
695	## What these tools share
696	
697	- **Times** are in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
698	- **One call is one undo step.**
699	- **The answer** is `ok: true`, the ids of anything created, and a `project` summary. A call that changes nothing says so and leaves no undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
700	- **Rates** run from ×0.1 to ×1000, where 1 is normal speed. See each tool for what it does with a rate outside that.

5	---
6	title: "Check the picture: render_frame"
7	description: "Render one frame of the finished timeline so an agent can see its work, choose the file it writes, draw grade and HDR variants, and measure the scopes."
8	---
9	
10	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
11	
12	`render_frame` draws one frame of the finished timeline, so an agent can see what it has done. It goes through the same composition and compositor an export uses, so the picture is what the file will contain at that moment, not a preview of it.
13	
14	<AtAGlance
15	  menu="File ▸ Save Frame…"
16	  keys="⌥⌘E"
17	  tools="render_frame"
18	/>
19	
20	## Render a frame
21	
22	With no arguments it draws the frame under the playhead at the canvas's size and writes a PNG to a temporary file.
23	
24	```json
25	{ "t": 1200000, "path": "/tmp/shot.png", "max_width": 960 }
26	```
27	
28	The picture comes back two ways: as an image the model can see, and as a file on disk. The text beside it says what was drawn and ends by naming the file:
29	
30	```
31	Frame at 1200000 ticks of a 1920×1080 px canvas, rendered at 960×540 px. Written to /tmp/shot.png.
32	```
33	
34	It uses the same writer as [**File ▸ Save Frame…**](/export/save-frame/), so a PNG from either one is identical, byte for byte.
35	
36	With a [nest](/mcp/nests/) open, it draws that nest at its own size, from its own zero, without the nest clip's position, scale or opacity. It takes no `scope`, so open the nest with `set_scope` to look inside.
37	
38	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does | Default |
39	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
40	| [`t`](#t) | integer | No | The moment to render, in ticks. | The playhead |
41	| [`path`](#path) | string | No | Where to write the file. | A temporary file |
42	| [`format`](#format) | string | No | `png`, `jpeg` or `heic`. | From the path, else `png` |
43	| [`max_width`](#max_width) | integer | No | Caps the width in pixels, 16 to 8192. | The canvas's width |
44	| [`burn_in_timecode`](#burn_in_timecode) | boolean | No | Draws the project timecode over the picture. | `false` |
45	| [`ungraded`](#ungraded) | boolean | No | Draws every clip as if it weren't graded. | `false` |
46	| [`selection`](#selection) | integer | No | Draws what an adjustment clip's qualifier selects. | None |
47	| [`sdr_version`](#sdr_version) | boolean | No | Draws an HDR project's SDR version. | `false` |
48	| [`waveform`](#waveform-parade-and-histogram) | boolean | No | Also measures the waveform. | `false` |
49	| [`parade`](#waveform-parade-and-histogram) | boolean | No | Also measures the RGB parade. | `false` |
50	| [`histogram`](#waveform-parade-and-histogram) | boolean | No | Also measures the histogram. | `false` |
51	| [`vectorscope`](#vectorscope-and-vectorscope_zoom) | boolean | No | Also measures the vectorscope. | `false` |
52	| [`vectorscope_zoom`](#vectorscope-and-vectorscope_zoom) | integer | No | 1, 2 or 4. Needs `vectorscope`. | 1 |
53	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on. | The frontmost project |
54	
55	## Choose the moment and the file
56	
57	### `t`
58	
59	The moment to render, in ticks, 600,000 to the second. It's rounded to the project's frame grid. Leave it out for the playhead. A time before zero draws the first frame, and a time past the end is refused.
60	
61	With a nest open, `t` and the playhead are the nest's own time.
62	
63	### `path`
64	
65	Where to write the file, for example `~/Desktop/shot.png`. The folder must already exist, because Frame Job won't create one. An empty `path` is refused.
66	
67	Leave it out for a temporary file. Either way, the last sentence of the text names the file written.
68	
69	### `format`
70	
71	The kind of file to write.
72	
73	| `format` | What you get |
74	| --- | --- |
75	| `png` | Lossless, keeping the canvas's transparency. |
76	| `jpeg` | Quality 0.9. JPEG has no transparency, so a transparent canvas is flattened onto black, and the text always says so. |
77	| `heic` | Quality 0.9, keeping the canvas's transparency. |
78	
79	With no `format`, the path's extension decides: `.jpg` and `.jpeg` both mean JPEG, and `.heic` means HEIC. Any other path writes a PNG.
80	
81	An explicit `format` wins, and the path's extension is replaced rather than added to, so `{"path": "shot.jpg", "format": "png"}` writes `shot.png`. Only an extension Frame Job knows is replaced: `Talk v1.2` becomes `Talk v1.2.png`, not `Talk v1.png`. A JPEG always ends `.jpg`, so `shot.jpeg` is written as `shot.jpg`.
82	
83	`jpg` also works as a `format`, and capitals don't matter.
84	
85	### `max_width`
86	
87	Caps the image's width in pixels, from 16 to 8192. The picture keeps its shape and is never made larger than the canvas. Leave it out for the canvas's own size.
88	
89	A smaller frame is quicker to send and to look at. The [scopes](#measure-the-frame) measure the frame as written, so their counts cover fewer pixels too.
90	
91	## Change what's drawn
92	
93	These four draw something other than the plain picture. The view switches in the window never reach this tool or an export, so an agent asks here.
94	
95	### `burn_in_timecode`
96	
97	Draws the project timecode over the picture, on top of everything, as the export sheet's **Burn in timecode** does. It's the project's own timecode, in the toolbar's spelling. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/).
98	
99	### `ungraded`
100	
101	Draws every clip as if it weren't graded: Light, Color, wheels and curves neutral, and no look. It's the picture **View ▸ Show Ungraded** gives. See [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/).
102	
103	### `selection`
104	
105	Takes an adjustment clip's id and draws what its qualifier selects, in place of grading. It's the picture **View ▸ Show Selection** gives.
106	
107	- White is fully graded, and black is untouched.
108	- It's the blurred selection when the qualifier has a blur, and it's multiplied by any matte cutting the clip.
109	- The clip's strength isn't applied.
110	- Every layer in front of the clip is left out.
111	- Where the clip isn't on the frame, the picture is black.
112	
113	Frame Job won't do this for any other kind of clip. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).
114	
115	### `sdr_version`
116	
117	Draws an [HDR project's](/hdr/dynamic-range/) SDR version, the picture **View ▸ Show SDR Version** gives. White titles come back near white, and highlights above reference white roll off. It's what the SDR exports and JPEG frames hold.
118	
119	In an SDR project it changes nothing, and the frame comes out identical. See [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/).
120	
121	## Measure the frame
122	
123	Each scope argument measures the rendered frame through the same analyser as the [**View ▸ Scopes**](/color/scopes/) panel, so the two can't count differently. The text gives the headline figures, and a JSON file beside the image holds the counts, named after it: `shot.png` gets `shot.png.waveform.json`.
124	
125	The scopes read the frame as it was drawn, so `max_width`, `burn_in_timecode`, `ungraded` and `selection` all change what they count.
126	
127	If the measurement can't run, the call comes back as an error, but the image is already written and the error names it: "Wrote …, but its waveform could not be measured: the GPU pass did not run."
128	
129	### `waveform`, `parade` and `histogram`
130	
131	- **`waveform`** measures luma. The text gives the share of pixels clipping high and low.
132	- **`parade`** measures R′, G′ and B′ the way the waveform measures luma. The text gives the share clipping high and low for each channel.
133	- **`histogram`** counts R′, G′, B′ and Y′ at 256 levels. The text gives the share clipping high and low, read from Y′.
134	
135	For example: "Waveform: highlights clipped in 0.4 % of pixels, shadows in 0.0 %; its 256 × 256 counts are in …". A pixel clips high at level 255 and low at level 0.
136	
137	| JSON key | `waveform` | `parade` | `histogram` |
138	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
139	| `width`, `height` | The frame measured | The frame measured | The frame measured |
140	| `levels` | 256 | 256 | 256 |
141	| `columns` | 256 | 256 | |
142	| `counts` | 256 column bins, each 256 levels | The same, under `red`, `green` and `blue` | |
143	| `red`, `green`, `blue`, `luma` | | | 256 counts each |
144	| `clipped_high`, `clipped_low` | Pixels clipping | Pixels clipping, by channel | Pixels clipping, by Y′ |
145	| `marks_high`, `marks_low` | The column bins where at least 0.5 % of the column clips | The same, by channel | |
146	| `highlights`, `shadows` | Percentages | | Percentages |
147	
148	### `vectorscope` and `vectorscope_zoom`
149	
150	`vectorscope` measures Rec. 709 Cb and Cr of the encoded values in 256 × 256 bins centred on neutral, bin 128. The text gives the share of pixels that are neutral.
151	
152	`vectorscope_zoom` is 1, 2 or 4, like the 1×, 2× and 4× cells on a [vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) slot, and it needs `vectorscope: true`. Zooming spreads a near-grey picture over more bins. At 2 and 4, a pixel off the plot isn't counted, and the text also gives the share that lie off it.
153	
154	| JSON key | What it holds |
155	| --- | --- |
156	| `width`, `height` | The frame measured. |
157	| `bins`, `centre` | 256 and 128. |
158	| `matrix`, `values` | `Rec. 709` and `encoded`. |
159	| `counts` | 256 arrays by Cr bin, each indexed by Cb bin. |
160	| `neutral` | Pixels in the neutral bin. |
161	| `zoom` | The zoom. |
162	| `off_plot` | Pixels left off the plot. Always 0 at 1. |
163	| `targets` | The six 75 % colour targets, `R`, `Mg`, `B`, `Cy`, `G` and `Yl`, each `[cb, cr]` in bins at this zoom, or `null` off the plot. |
164	| `skin_line_degrees` | The skin line's angle. |
165	
166	## Read what the answer says
167	
168	The text always starts with the frame's time and sizes and ends with "Written to …". Anything else worth saying sits between the two.
169	
170	### Graphic problems in the answer
171	
172	When a [graphic](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/) in the frame had a problem, the answer names it with its frame and the diagnostic:
173	
174	- `Graphic "lower-third" failed at frame 12: …`
175	- `Graphic "lower-third" warned at frame 12: …`
176	- `Graphic "lower-third" does not compile: …`
177	
178	A failed graphic draws its error card in the picture.
179	
180	### Waiting for cutout masks
181	
182	A clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) waits up to 30 s for the masks the frame needs. Frame Job starts making them as soon as the cutout is set, on your Mac.
183	
184	Past 30 s the clip is drawn whole, and the answer says so: "Clip 12 is drawn uncut: its person masks were not ready within 30 s." For a picture with its subject set to foreground, it says "its foreground masks".
185	
186	So after setting a cutout, read that sentence before trusting the frame. [`analyze_cutout`](/mcp/tools-analysis/) can wait for the masks first.
187	
188	### A cursor that can't be drawn
189	
190	A screen recording's cursor is drawn from its cursor file. When the file can't be read, the clip draws without one and the answer says "The cursor of media 5 is not drawn: …".
191	
192	## Frames from an HDR project
193	
194	In an [HLG project](/hdr/dynamic-range/), the frame depends on the format:
195	
196	| What you ask for | What you get |
197	| --- | --- |
198	| `png` | 16-bit, labelled BT.2100 HLG |
199	| `heic` | 10-bit, labelled BT.2100 HLG |
200	| `jpeg` | The project's SDR version, labelled BT.709 |
201	| Any format with `sdr_version` | The project's SDR version, labelled BT.709 |
202	
203	Scopes read the picture drawn. On the HLG picture they read the HLG signal, and on the SDR version they read as an SDR project's do.
204	
205	On the HLG signal:
206	
207	- Each scope's JSON adds `signal: "hlg"`.
208	- The waveform, parade and histogram JSON add `scale`: `unit` (`cd/m²`), `ticks` (each with `percent`, `level` and `nits`), `reference_white_percent` (75) and `clip_percent` (100).
209	- Luma takes Rec. 2020's weights, and the vectorscope takes Rec. 2020's matrix and targets.
210	- The text says so. The waveform's reads "reference white at 75 %, 203 cd/m², and 100 % at 1,000 cd/m²".
211	
212	See [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/) and [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/).
213	
214	## When it won't render
215	
216	Nothing is drawn in these cases, and the answer says why.
217	
218	| It says | What to do |
219	| --- | --- |
220	| "No frame at … Either the time is past the end of the timeline, the media is missing, or the timeline is empty." | Check `duration` and `missing_media` in [`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/). |
221	| "There is no folder at … to write into." | Create the folder, or choose another `path`. |
222	| "path must name a file to write — omit it for a temporary one." | The `path` was empty. |
223	| "format must be one of png, jpeg, heic (got …)." | Use one of the three. |
224	| "max_width must be 16…8192 px (got …)." | Use a width in range. |
225	| "selection must name an adjustment clip of this project; clip … is not one." | Pass an adjustment clip's id. An adjustment clip can't be inside a nest, so close any open nest first. |
226	| "vectorscope_zoom must be 1, 2 or 4 (got …)." | Use one of the three. |
227	| "vectorscope_zoom needs vectorscope: true." | Add `vectorscope: true`. |
228	
229	## Related
230	
231	- [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/)
232	- [Tools: rendering and export](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/)
233	- [Scopes](/color/scopes/)
234	- [A typical session](/mcp/typical-session/)
235	---
236	title: "Export: start, then poll"
237	description: Write a file from an agent, follow the job until it finishes, stop it, and read what the file holds.
238	---
239	
240	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
241	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
242	
243	Use these three tools to write the timeline to a file from an agent, follow the job and stop it. `export` doesn't wait for the file. It checks the request, puts a job on the Export Queue and returns at once, and the agent then asks how the job is going until it ends.
244	
245	<AtAGlance
246	  menu={['File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
247	  keys="⌘E"
248	  where="The export sheet's Add to Queue, and each row's Cancel in the Export Queue"
249	  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
250	/>
251	
252	## Write a file
253	
254	<Steps>
255	
256	1. Call `export` with a preset and a path. It returns straight away.
257	
258	   ```json
259	   { "preset": "h264", "path": "/Volumes/Edits/cut", "size": "1080p" }
260	   ```
261	
262	   ```json
263	   { "export_id": 3, "path": "/Volumes/Edits/cut.mp4", "status": "running" }
264	   ```
265	
266	2. Call `export_status` with that `export_id`, pause, and call it again until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
267	
268	3. Read the `done` result. It says what the file holds, including the loudness it measured and any warnings.
269	
270	</Steps>
271	
272	To stop the job, call `cancel_export`. The job shows in **Window ▸ Export Queue** like any other, but the window doesn't open by itself.
273	
274	## Export
275	
276	`export` does what **File ▸ Export…** does with **Add to Queue**, and it writes the file the same way, so an agent's file and a person's match. It takes the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)'s controls in the sheet's own terms, apart from the frame rate.
277	
278	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
279	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
280	| `preset` | string | Yes | The encoding: a container and a codec. See [Presets](#presets). |
281	| `path` | string | Yes | Where to write, such as `~/Movies/cut.mp4`. See [Path handling](#path-handling). |
282	| `size` | string or `[width, height]` | No | The output size. See [Size](#size). |
283	| `range` | string | No | `project` for the whole timeline, or `in_out` for the in and out range. See [Range](#range). |
284	| `video_bitrate` | integer | No | Target video rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
285	| `audio_bitrate` | integer | No | Target AAC or Opus rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
286	| `loudness_lufs` | number | No | Normalise the whole mix to this loudness, −70 to 0. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
287	| `peak_dbtp` | number | No | The master limiter's ceiling, −20 to 0. See [Peak dBTP](#peak-dbtp). |
288	| `audio_bits` | integer | No | 16 or 24, for WAV and AIFF. See [Audio bits](#audio-bits). |
289	| `stems` | string | No | `tracks` or `names`, to write stems beside an audio mix. See [Stems](#stems). |
290	| `burn_in_timecode` | boolean | No | Draw the project timecode over the picture, on top of everything. Off by default. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
291	| `dynamic_range` | string | No | `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`, in an HLG project. See [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range). |
292	| `encoder_speed` | string | No | `faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`, for AV1. See [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
293	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to export, as `get_project` reports it. Without it, the frontmost project. |
294	
295	It returns `{export_id, path, status}`. `path` is the file that will be written, with `~` expanded and the extension corrected. `status` is `running` if the job started at once, or `queued` if it's waiting.
296	
297	Jobs in the queue run one at a time, behind anything already there. A job writes the project as it stood when `export` was called, so later edits don't reach it. Calling `export` pauses playback in that project's window.
298	
299	`export` takes no `scope`. With a [nest](/mcp/nests/) open it still writes the project's timeline, not the nest's.
300	
301	## Export status
302	
303	`export_status` reports how a job is going, as its row in the Export Queue does, and it never waits. Pass the `export_id`, which is an integer of 1 or more.
304	
305	Every result carries `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed`, the seconds since `export` was called, or from then to the finish once the job has ended. The rest depends on the status.
306	
307	| `status` | Also carries |
308	| --- | --- |
309	| `queued` | `waiting` while an AV1 or VP9 job is held for memory. `estimated_seconds` on `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`. |
310	| `running` | `progress`, from 0 to 1. `phase` while the export names one, which is "Measuring loudness…" during the first pass over the mix. `estimated_seconds` on the same four presets. |
311	| `done` | What the file holds, in the next table. |
312	| `failed` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
313	| `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
314	
315	`estimated_seconds` is the export sheet's estimate of the whole export in whole seconds, and it's only an estimate.
316	
317	`waiting` is a sentence such as "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.1 GB of the 8.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 7.0 GB." AV1 and VP9 exports may hold a quarter of this Mac's memory between them, though a job with no other running always starts. While one is held, a later job in the queue may run first.
318	
319	A `done` result adds these keys.
320	
321	| Key | What it holds |
322	| --- | --- |
323	| `ok` | `true`. |
324	| `bytes` | The file's size. |
325	| `preset`, `container`, `codec` | What was written. |
326	| `width`, `height` | The file's size in pixels. These are reported on audio presets too, where they mean nothing. |
327	| `fps` | The rate as `[num, den]`, such as `[30, 1]`. |
328	| `start`, `duration` | The part of the timeline written, in [ticks](/mcp/units-and-ids/). |
329	| `burn_in_timecode` | Whether the argument was on. |
330	| `dynamic_range` | The picture written: `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`. Only for a video preset in an HLG project. |
331	| `encoder_speed` | The speed used. Only on `av1` and `av1_webm`. |
332	| `audio_bits` | The depth written. Only on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. |
333	| `stems` | `[{name, tracks, path}]`, one per file beside the mix. Only when `stems` was asked for. |
334	| `loudness` | What the mix measured. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
335	| `graphic_warnings` | `[{name, frame, message}]`, each distinct warning a graphic gave while the file was drawn. Collecting stops after 64 distinct reports, so a noisy graphic's list can be cut short. `frame` is the graphic's own frame, or `null`. Absent when there were none. |
336	| `cursor_warnings` | `[{media, path, message}]`, each media whose cursor file couldn't be drawn. Its clips were written without a cursor. Absent when there were none. |
337	
338	## Cancel export
339	
340	`cancel_export` stops a job, as the row's **Cancel** does, and returns what `export_status` would. Pass the `export_id`.
341	
342	| The job is | What happens |
343	| --- | --- |
344	| Queued | It's cancelled before it starts. The result reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled before it started." |
345	| Running | It stops and its half-written file is removed. The result may still read `running` until writing has stopped, and `export_status` then reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled." |
346	| Finished | It's left alone, and its file stays. The result is the finished job's. |
347	
348	## Export id and its lifetime
349	
350	An `export_id` is known until Frame Job quits. Removing a finished row from the Export Queue, or choosing **Clear Finished**, doesn't lose it, so an agent can still read how that job ended.
351	
352	An id belongs to the launch, not to a project, so `export_status` and `cancel_export` don't need `project`. Only ids that `export` returned are known. A job a person queued from the sheet has no id an agent can follow. Any other number returns the error "No export this launch has export_id 7 — ids come from export and last until Frame Job quits."
353	
354	## Refusals and failures
355	
356	A problem Frame Job can see from the request comes back from `export` itself as an error, and nothing is queued.
357	
358	| The request | What stops it |
359	| --- | --- |
360	| An empty timeline | "There is nothing on the timeline to export." |
361	| A folder that doesn't exist | "There is no folder at … to write into." Frame Job never creates the folder. |
362	| An unknown preset | The error lists all the presets. |
363	| An unknown `size`, or one it can't read | The error lists the sizes. See [Size](#size). |
364	| `range` of `in_out` with no range set | "This project has no in/out range — set one with set_range `{start, end}`, or export with range \"project\"." |
365	| A number out of range, or a word it doesn't know | The error names the argument and the value. |
366	| An option the preset doesn't have | See [Audio bits](#audio-bits), [Stems](#stems), [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range) and [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
367	| A graphic clip in the range with no module, or a module that doesn't compile | "The export was not started: the graphic "…" does not compile — …. Fix the module and export again." A clip with no module reads "has no module in graphics/" in place of "does not compile — …". It names each graphic and its first error, and it covers graphics inside nests. An audio-only preset draws no graphics, so it isn't stopped by one. |
368	
369	Anything that goes wrong after that comes back from `export_status` as `failed`, with the sentence in `reason`. Check for it even when `export` answered cleanly.
370	
371	| What went wrong | The `reason` |
372	| --- | --- |
373	| A size of another shape on a transparent preset | "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…". See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets). |
374	| A stem's file would be one of the project's media | "The stem “…” would replace media this project uses; export under another name." |
375	| A graphic fails while it's drawn | "The export was stopped at frame … of the graphic "…": …. No file was written." |
376	| A retimed clip's sound, an isolated voice or a voice effect couldn't be rendered | The sentence names the clip and the reason. |
377	| A cut-out clip's masks couldn't be made | "Clip …'s person masks could not be made: …." A picture cut out by **Foreground** says foreground masks. |
378	| A clip's gate, leveller or de-esser needs a loudness that hasn't been measured | "Clip …'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…". Wait for the clip's analysis, then export again. |
379	| This Mac has no encoder for the preset | "This Mac cannot export with the “…” preset." |
380	
381	A graphic's warnings are different: they don't stop the export, and they arrive as `graphic_warnings` in the `done` result.
382	
383	## Presets
384	
385	There are 15 presets, one per encoding. A preset says nothing about size. These are the rows of the sheet's **Format** control, described in [Choose a format](/export/formats/). A wrong id's error lists them all.
386	
387	| Preset | In the sheet | File | Picture | Sound |
388	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
389	| `h264` | H.264 (MP4) | `.mp4` | 8-bit. The sheet's first row. | AAC |
390	| `hevc` | HEVC (MP4) | `.mp4` | 8-bit | AAC |
391	| `hevc_alpha` | HEVC with Alpha (MOV) | `.mov` | 8-bit with transparency. Safari's transparent movie. | AAC |
392	| `hevc_10bit` | HEVC 10-bit (MP4) | `.mp4` | 10-bit | AAC |
393	| `av1` | AV1 (MP4) | `.mp4` | 10-bit | AAC |
394	| `av1_webm` | AV1 (WebM) | `.webm` | 10-bit | Opus |
395	| `vp9_webm` | VP9 (WebM) | `.webm` | 8-bit (Profile 0) for an SDR picture, 10-bit (Profile 2) for HLG and PQ. One speed. | Opus |
396	| `vp9_alpha_webm` | VP9 with Alpha (WebM) | `.webm` | Always 8-bit, with transparency. The transparent movie Chrome and Firefox play. | Opus |
397	| `prores_422` | ProRes 422 (MOV) | `.mov` | 10-bit. An editing master. | 16-bit LPCM |
398	| `prores_4444` | ProRes 4444 (MOV) | `.mov` | 12-bit with transparency. A master. | 16-bit LPCM |
399	| `audio_m4a` | Audio only (M4A) | `.m4a` | None | AAC |
400	| `audio_wav` | Audio only (WAV) | `.wav` | None | 48 kHz LPCM, 16 or 24 bits |
401	| `audio_aiff` | Audio only (AIFF) | `.aiff` | None | 48 kHz LPCM, 16 or 24 bits |
402	| `gif` | Animated GIF | `.gif` | 256 colours. Fits inside 480 × 270 unless `size` says otherwise. | None |
403	| `apng` | Animated PNG | `.png` | Lossless, with transparency. Fits inside 960 × 540 unless `size` says otherwise. | None |
404	
405	Macs before M3 can't play `av1` and `av1_webm` back.
406	
407	## Frame rate
408	
409	There's no frame-rate argument, so the sheet's [frame rate](/export/frame-rate/) control has no agent equivalent. An export runs at the project's rate, `gif` at 12.5 fps and `apng` at 25 fps. The `done` result's `fps` says which, with 12.5 fps as `[25, 2]`.
410	
411	## Path handling
412	
413	The folder must exist. A `~` at the start is expanded, and an existing file at the path is replaced.
414	
415	The file always ends in the preset's extension.
416	
417	| `path` | `preset` | Writes | Why |
418	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
419	| `cut.mp4` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | The extension is already right. |
420	| `cut` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | With no extension, it's added. |
421	| `cut.mov` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | A different media extension is replaced. |
422	| `Talk v1.2` | `h264` | `Talk v1.2.mp4` | Any other suffix stays part of the name. |
423	| `cut.webm` | `h264` | `cut.webm.mp4` | `.webm` isn't one of the extensions Frame Job replaces. |
424	| `cut.mp4` | `av1_webm` | `cut.webm` | `.mp4` is. |
425	
426	The extensions it replaces are `.mov`, `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.m4a`, `.mp3`, `.wav`, `.aif`, `.aiff`, `.caf`, `.framejob`, `.srt`, `.vtt`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.heic` and `.gif`. The returned `path` is always the file that gets written.
427	
428	## Size
429	
430	`size` is the sheet's **Size** control. See [Export size](/export/size/) for what the sizes mean to a person.
431	
432	| `size` | In the sheet | What it writes |
433	| --- | --- | --- |
434	| `document` | Document size | The project's own size. The default on every movie preset. |
435	| `2160p` | 4K | A short edge of 2160 pixels. |
436	| `1440p` | 1440p | A short edge of 1440 pixels. |
437	| `1080p` | 1080p | A short edge of 1080 pixels. |
438	| `720p` | 720p | A short edge of 720 pixels. |
439	| `preset` | GIF default, APNG default | The format's cap. `gif` and `apng` only, where it's the default. |
440	| `[width, height]` | Custom… | Exactly this size, from 16 to 8192 pixels on each edge. |
441	
442	The number is always the short edge, and the long edge follows the project's shape, rounded to an even number. A vertical project's `1080p` is 1080 × 1920. Every size means the same on every project, so a 1920 × 1080 project's `1080p` is its own size, and a size larger than the project scales it up.
443	
444	A movie is written at exactly the size asked for. If the shape differs from the project's by more than a pixel, the picture is letterboxed. Within a pixel, it fills the frame instead.
445	
446	- **Even edges.** Every preset but `prores_4444`, `gif` and `apng` needs even dimensions, so an odd width or height is written one pixel smaller. That covers `document` on a project with an odd edge. The `done` result's `width` and `height` are the file's.
447	- **GIF and APNG.** A size is a box the picture is fitted inside, keeping its shape and never scaling up. A vertical 1080 × 1920 project's GIF default comes out at 152 × 270.
448	- **Audio presets.** A size has no effect, and `preset` isn't one of their sizes.
449	- **Transparent movies.** A `[width, height]` of another shape fails. See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets).
450	
451	An unknown size returns an error with the list, for example "No export size is called "480p" for h264. The sizes are: document, 2160p, 1440p, 1080p, 720p — or pass [width, height]." A custom size outside 16 to 8192 pixels is an error too. It isn't clamped.
452	
453	## Range
454	
455	`range` is the sheet's **Range** control. `project`, the default, writes the whole timeline. `in_out` writes the range set with `set_range`, and `export` returns an error when there's no range. See [Export a range](/export/range/).
456	
457	The range is snapped to the export's frame grid and kept inside the project. A range that comes to nothing is an error too.
458	
459	`burn_in_timecode` shows project time even in a range export, so a file written from 00:00:10:00 begins at 00:00 with a burn-in that reads 00:00:10:00.
460	
461	## Exact bitrates
462	
463	The sheet offers [quality](/export/quality/) tiers. An agent sets the rates directly, in bits per second, so 8 Mbps is `8000000`. Each must be a whole number from 1 to 4,294,967,295.
464	
465	`video_bitrate` is the target video rate. Without it, Frame Job works out a rate from the frame size and frame rate. ProRes, GIF and APNG ignore it, because ProRes is fixed by its profile and the other two have no bitrate.
466	
467	On the AV1 and VP9 presets it works differently:
468	
469	- **`av1` and `av1_webm`.** It's a soft cap. The encoder works at a constant quality matched to HEVC at that rate, and the file usually comes in well under it. Very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over. Without it, the quality is matched to HEVC at 0.07 bits per pixel per frame.
470	- **`vp9_webm`.** It's a soft cap too, matched to HEVC, or HEVC 10-bit in an HDR export. Up to about 1.15 times over was measured.
471	- **`vp9_alpha_webm`.** It's the same soft cap on the picture's stream alone. The transparency's stream comes on top, at a constant quality.
472	
473	`audio_bitrate` is the AAC or Opus rate, 192 kbps when absent. Opus takes the nearest rate its encoder offers. ProRes, WAV and AIFF ignore it, because they write LPCM.
474	
475	## The loudness report
476	
477	Every export with sound measures its own mix and reports it as `loudness` in the `done` result, normalised or not. GIF and APNG have no sound, and a timeline with no sound has nothing to measure, so `loudness` is absent from both.
478	
479	`loudness_lufs` normalises the whole mix to an integrated loudness, from −70 to 0. The sheet's [Loudness](/export/loudness/) rows are −14 for streaming, −16 for podcasts and −23 for EBU R 128 broadcast, and an agent can ask for any value, such as −14.5. The export measures itself first, then applies one gain to everything, through the master limiter. The file lands on the target with its loudest peaks limited, rather than the whole mix held down. GIF and APNG ignore it.
480	
481	| Key | What it holds |
482	| --- | --- |
483	| `summary` | The same line the queue row and the progress sheet show, such as "Peak −1.0 dBTP · −16.0 LUFS", with " · peaks limited by 8.6 dB" when the limiter took 0.05 dB or more. |
484	| `integrated_lufs` | The file's integrated loudness. Absent when it has none, and `summary` then says "loudness not measurable". |
485	| `true_peak_dbtp` | The file's true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
486	| `sample_peak_dbfs` | The file's sample peak, never above the true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
487	| `gain_db` | The gain applied to reach the target. |
488	| `ceiling_dbtp` | The master limiter's ceiling. |
489	| `limited_db` | How far the limiter turned the loudest peak down. |
490	| `capped_by_gain` | `true` when the +40 dB limit on the gain decided it, so the file may be short of the target. |
491	| `target_lufs` | The `loudness_lufs` asked for. Absent when none was. |
492	
493	A programme shorter than one 400 ms measuring block, or one too quiet to pass the standard's gate, has a peak and no integrated loudness. Digital silence reads "Silent" in `summary`.
494	
495	## Peak dBTP
496	
497	Every export with sound goes through a master limiter, so the file's true peak stays at or under a ceiling. `peak_dbtp` sets that ceiling, from −20 to 0. It's −1 when absent, which is the sheet's fixed value. 0 is the loosest, and there's no way to turn the limiter off.
498	
499	You can pass it with or without `loudness_lufs`. `limited_db` in the [report](#the-loudness-report) says how far the limiter turned the loudest peak down.
500	
501	## Audio bits
502	
503	`audio_bits` is the sheet's [Bit depth](/export/bit-depth/) control: 16, the default, or 24. It's rounded once from the mix and never dithered, and the `done` result repeats it.
504	
505	It works on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` only. On any other preset `export` returns the error "h264 has no bit depth; audio_bits applies to audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset. ProRes keeps 16-bit sound. Any other number is an error, whatever the preset.
506	
507	## Stems
508	
509	`stems` also writes [stems](/export/stems/) beside the mix, on `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. It's the sheet's **Stems** control.
510	
511	| `stems` | What it writes |
512	| --- | --- |
513	| `tracks` | One file per heard track. |
514	| `names` | One file per track name. Heard tracks whose names match, ignoring case, share a file, and an unnamed track gets its own. |
515	
516	A track is heard when it has sound in it and isn't muted or silenced by another track's solo. Each stem is named `<file> - <track name>.<ext>`, beside the mix, so `mix.wav` and a track called Voice give `mix - Voice.wav`. An unnamed track is `Track N`, and [Stem file names](/export/stems/#stem-file-names) has the other cases.
517	
518	A stem holds its tracks' sound before the master, with no loudness gain and no limiter, so the stems add up to the mix wherever the master changed nothing. Any file already at a stem's name is replaced.
519	
520	The `done` result lists each one as `stems [{name, tracks, path}]`. `tracks` holds the ids of the timeline tracks in that stem.
521	
522	- On any other preset `export` returns the error "h264 has no stems; stems applies to audio_m4a, audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset.
523	- With no track heard, the error is "stems: no track is heard, so there is no stem to write".
524	- If a stem's file would be one of the project's media, the job fails before any stem is written, and `export_status` gives the reason.
525	- A failed or cancelled job leaves neither the mix nor any stem behind.
526	
527	## Dynamic range
528	
529	`dynamic_range` chooses the picture an [HLG project](/hdr/dynamic-range/) writes. It's the sheet's **Dynamic Range** control.
530	
531	| `dynamic_range` | What it writes |
532	| --- | --- |
533	| `hlg` | BT.2100 HLG, with no Dolby Vision. The default on the presets that carry HDR. |
534	| `pq` | HDR10: BT.2100 PQ at 1,000 cd/m², with a P3-D65 mastering display of 0.005–1,000 cd/m², MaxCLL 1,000 and MaxFALL 0. |
535	| `sdr` | The project's SDR version. |
536	
537	The presets that carry HDR are `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422` and `prores_4444`. Every other video preset in an HLG project writes the SDR version, `vp9_alpha_webm` included, and audio presets ignore the argument.
538	
539	- `hlg` or `pq` on another video preset returns the error "h264 is 8-bit and writes the SDR version; export dynamic_range "pq" as hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, prores_422 or prores_4444".
540	- `hlg` or `pq` in an SDR project returns the error "dynamic_range "pq" needs an HLG project; set_canvas output "hlg" first".
541	- `sdr` in an SDR project changes nothing.
542	
543	Once a job is `done`, `dynamic_range` in the result names the picture that was written. An SDR project's result has no such key.
544	
545	## Encoder speed
546	
547	`encoder_speed` trades export time for file size on `av1` and `av1_webm`. It's the sheet's [Speed](/export/encoder-speed/) control, and the `done` result names the one used.
548	
549	| `encoder_speed` | SVT-AV1 preset | What it does |
550	| --- | --- | --- |
551	| `faster` | 8 | The quickest. |
552	| `balanced` | 6 | The default. |
553	| `smaller` | 4 | The smallest file for the picture, and the slowest. |
554	
555	On every other preset `export` returns the error "h264 has no encoder speed; encoder_speed applies to av1 and av1_webm", naming the preset. That includes `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`, which have one speed.
556	
557	## Transparent presets
558	
559	Four presets keep a transparent canvas transparent: `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha`, `vp9_alpha_webm` and `apng`. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). A GIF can show a fully transparent pixel, but it has no alpha channel, so nothing partial survives.
560	
561	On the three movie presets, a `[width, height]` of a different shape from the canvas can't be written, because the padding would destroy the alpha channel. `export` queues the job, and `export_status` then reads `failed` with a reason that names both sizes. The shape is judged after an odd edge is evened, and within a pixel the picture fills the frame, so a size in the canvas's own proportions always works, at any scale. Every named size already has the canvas's shape.
562	
563	`apng` fits its picture inside the size instead, so this doesn't apply to it.
