592	## Record the screen
593	
594	The smallest call names only `seconds`:
595	
596	```json
597	{ "seconds": 30 }
598	```
599	
600	That records the main display for 30 seconds with its system sound, leaves Frame Job's own windows out of the picture, and lands the movie at the playhead of the front project. A recording then goes through these stages:
601	
602	- **It starts at once.** There's no countdown and no panel.
603	- **It writes to disk.** The file goes to `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`, named for example `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov`, and it's never stored inside the project. A name that's already taken gets ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on.
604	- **It lands.** The movie becomes ordinary media, and a clip goes at the playhead on the front track of whatever is open, a [nest](/mcp/nests/) included. When that track has no room there, Frame Job adds a new track in front of everything. This is one undo step, **Add Recording**.
605	- **It answers.** The call returns once the recording is finished, imported and placed. See [What it answers](#what-it-answers).
606	
607	With no project open, the recording opens as a new untitled project instead, and `landed` reads `new_project`. Its canvas takes the movie's size and `rate`. Later calls address that project with `project` set to the recording's path, which is the path `get_project` reports for it. If the target project closes while the recording runs, the same thing happens and the note says so.
608	
609	Only one recording runs at a time, whoever started it. A second one is refused with "A recording is already in progress."
610	
611	:::note
612	The built-in [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) can't call `record_screen`. Recording stays with a person at the Record button, or an agent connected from outside.
613	:::
614	
615	[Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) has the landing in full, and it's the same for both.

## The arguments

Only `seconds` is required. The sections further down cover the arguments for [voice-overs](#record-a-voice-over), [cameras](#record-a-camera-alone) and the [steps after landing](#run-steps-after-it-lands).

### Length and source

| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seconds` | number | Required | How long to record, from 1 to 600 seconds. It's wall-clock time, so a [pause](#a-person-can-pause-or-stop-it) shortens what's recorded. |
| `source` | `screen`, `voice_over` or `camera` | `screen` | What's recorded. See [Choose a source](#choose-a-source). |

### Display or window

| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `display` | whole number, 0 or more | `0` | Which display, as an index into the displays that can be shared, 0 being the main one. Can't be used with `window`. |
| `window` | whole number | None | The id of one window to record on its own, at that window's own size, instead of a display. Can't be used with `display`. |
| `include_framejob_windows` | boolean | `false` | Puts Frame Job's own windows, the editor and the preview, in a display recording. By default they're left out. With `window` it changes nothing. Frame Job's own sound stays out either way. |
| `size` | `nominal` or `best`, in any case | `nominal` | `nominal` records a display's point size, and `best` its pixel size, twice the points on a Retina display. An odd dimension is rounded up to even. |
| `rate` | `30` or `60` | `60` | The most frames a second the file may hold, and the canvas rate of a new project the recording opens as. |

A screen recording's frame rate is whatever the screen did, because a frame arrives only when something changes. A mostly still screen reports a low, fractional rate. That's the file and not a fault, and the picture holds its last frame to the end of the sound.

### Sound

| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `system_audio` | boolean | `true` | Records what the Mac plays as the movie's one stereo 48 kHz track. It takes in every app but Frame Job, so the timeline can play meanwhile and stay out of it. `false` writes a movie with no audio track, and `has_audio` reads false. |
| `microphone` | boolean | `false` | Also records the default microphone, to a second file beside the movie named `<movie name> (Microphone).m4a`. |

The microphone's file lands as its own clip on a new track at the back named **Microphone**, lined up with the picture by the measured `mic_offset`. When the microphone began first and there's no room for it there, the clip's head is trimmed rather than the clip landing late.

A microphone that fails doesn't fail the recording. The picture lands, that stretch has no `mic_path`, and `mic_problem` and the note say why. See [System audio and the microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/).

### Pointer and keys

| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | `separate` or `in_picture` | `separate` | `separate` keeps the pointer out of the movie, and Frame Job draws it on the clip from the cursor file, where you can restyle it. `in_picture` has macOS burn the pointer into the movie. |
| `show_clicks` | boolean | `false` | Shows each mouse click. With `in_picture`, a circle is drawn around each click into the movie. With `separate`, the clips land with click ripples on, drawn by Frame Job. |
| `keys` | `off` or `shortcuts` | `off` | `shortcuts` writes keyboard shortcuts into the cursor files, and needs the Input Monitoring permission. |

Every display or window recording writes a cursor file beside each movie, named `<movie name>.fjcursor`, holding the pointer's path, its clicks and scrolls. A problem with it never fails the recording. `segments` reports it as `cursor_problem`, and the note repeats it. A `separate` stretch with no cursor file has no pointer at all, and the note ends "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."

With `keys: "shortcuts"`, the file records each shortcut pressed with ⌘ or ⌃, or with ⌥ and an arrow, Delete, Forward Delete, Return, Enter, Tab or Esc, spelled like `cmd+shift+4`. Every other key is a mark of the time alone, never which key was typed. Nothing is written while an app holds secure input. See [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) and [The cursor in a recording](/recording/cursor/).

### Where it goes

| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings` | A folder to record into, created if it doesn't exist. It names the folder and never the file, and the answer's `path` is the file that was written. A blank string means the default folder. |
| `project` | string | The front project | The open project to land in, as `get_project` reports its path. One that names nothing open is refused, and it never turns into a new project. |
| `place` | boolean | `true` | Puts clips on the timeline, in one undo step with the media. `false` adds the recording to the media list only, and the note says to place it with `add_clip`. |

In a new project `place: false` has no effect, because the picture is the document. Its clips are on the timeline, one for each stretch and the first at 0, and the note says so.

## Record a voice-over

## It never asks for a permission

`record_screen` reads each permission and never requests one. It never shows a system prompt, never opens the window picker and never opens System Settings. A person grants them in the panel, usually by pressing **Record** in **File ▸ New Recording…** once. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).

| Permission | When it's read | What a missing one answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Screen Recording | Any `screen` recording | "Screen Recording is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording, then relaunch." |
| Microphone | `microphone: true` or `source: "voice_over"` | "The microphone is not granted to Frame Job (status: denied)." and the Microphone pane. With status `notDetermined`, it says to press Record in **File ▸ New Recording…** once. The status may also read `restricted`. |
| Camera | `source: "camera"` or `camera` | "The camera is not granted to Frame Job (status: denied)." and the Camera pane. With status `notDetermined`, it says to press Record with the Camera source once. |
| Input Monitoring | `keys: "shortcuts"` | "Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring." |

A Frame Job launched from a shell runs under the terminal's permissions, not its own. Each of these answers then also names the launching process by its pid, and says the permission that counts is that application's, or to relaunch with `open -a "Frame Job"`.

:::caution
macOS periodically asks whether to keep letting Frame Job record, and neither Frame Job nor the tool can see that alert. A capture waiting behind it looks like a hang. When a start or a finish times out, the answer says an alert may be waiting on the screen. Answer it and call again.
:::

## What's checked first

Refusals come in a fixed order, with the caller's own mistakes first, so a mistake is answered even with no permission at all.

1. `seconds` missing or outside 1 to 600.
2. `source` unknown, then the arguments that source can't take, then `microphone: false` with a voice-over.
3. `display` with `window`, or a `display` or `window` that isn't a valid number.
4. `rate` or `size` outside its values.
5. `keys` or `cursor` outside its values.
6. `enhance` without a microphone, then with `place: false`.
7. `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing`, in that order, each with `place: false`, and the last two without `keys: "shortcuts"`.
8. `camera_layout` outside its values, then `camera_layout` and `camera_cutout: true` with `place: false`.
9. The Microphone permission.
10. The Input Monitoring permission.
11. A `project` that names nothing open.
12. For a camera, the camera lookup, then `camera_format`, then the Camera permission.
13. For a screen, the Screen Recording permission.
14. The display or window lookup. A window that can't be shared answers "No window with id 123 is shareable." An index past the last display answers "display must be 0…1 (got 3); 2 displays are shareable."

When the console is locked or every display is asleep, step 14 answers "No display is shareable right now — the console is locked or every display is asleep; nothing can be recorded until one is."

After those, a call with a microphone needs a default microphone, or it answers "No microphone is available." Then the recording starts.

## How long the call takes

| Stage | How long |
| --- | --- |
| Starting | Up to 20 seconds, then "The recording did not start within 20 s." |
| Recording | `seconds`, plus about a second to start and finish. |
| Finishing | Up to about 75 s more if the files are slow to close, and 60 s more for each further stretch of a paused recording. |
| Finishing, with a camera beside the screen | Up to about 105 s more, and 90 s more for each further stretch, because each camera file is read too. |
| Landing | Up to 20 seconds, while a drag in the target project ends. |
| [Steps after landing](#what-they-wait-for) | Up to 5 minutes for each wait. |

A finish that times out answers with every movie it still holds, then the camera files, because they may yet finish on their own. If a drag outlasts its wait, the answer names the files too, which are on disk either way:

"The recording was saved at `<path>` but could not be added: …"

Calls run one at a time, so a recording holds up the next call until it answers. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).

## A person can pause or stop it

While an agent records, the same [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) appears as for the panel, so a person at the Mac can pause, resume or stop it. **File ▸ Pause Recording** and **File ▸ Stop Recording** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>) work too. An agent has no tool to pause or resume.

- **Stop** ends the call early and the recording still lands, with `stopped_by: "stopped"` and a `duration` shorter than `seconds`. That's the same value the tool's own stop gives, so the short `duration` is what tells the two apart.
- **Pause** shortens what the call records, because `seconds` keeps running. The paused time is in no file, and `pauses` counts the presses, including a pause with no resume before the stop.

A paused recording is a sequence of files, one for each stretch between a start or a resume and a pause or the stop. Each is named by its own start time and, with a microphone, carries its own microphone file. Every stretch lands as its own clip on one track, touching the one before, and each microphone file as its own clip on the **Microphone** track at its own offset.

---
title: "Tools: rendering and export"
description: "The agent tools that render one frame of the timeline, start an export, follow it on the Export Queue and stop it."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These tools turn the timeline into pictures and files. `render_frame` is how an agent sees what it has done, and `export`, `export_status` and `cancel_export` write the finished file.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Save Frame…', 'File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
  keys={['⌥⌘E', '⌘E']}
  tools={['render_frame', 'export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
  needs="A client connected over MCP, or the Assistant tab."
/>

This page is the quick reference. [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/) and [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/) have every argument in full, with what the agent gets back and what to do when a call fails.

Every tool here also takes `project`, the path of an open project. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/). `export_status` and `cancel_export` accept it but don't use it, because an `export_id` belongs to the launch, not to a project. None of the four takes `scope`.

## `render_frame`

Renders one frame of the finished timeline as a picture the model can see and a file on disk. It's drawn the way an export draws it, so it shows what the file will hold at that moment. Use it before and after every edit. It's the same writer as **File ▸ Save Frame…**, so a PNG written here and one saved from the menu are byte-identical. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).

With no arguments, it draws the frame under the playhead at the canvas's size and writes a PNG to a temporary file. Every argument is optional.

| To set | Use |
| --- | --- |
| The moment | [`t`](/mcp/render-frame/#t), in ticks. Default: the playhead. |
| The file | [`path`](/mcp/render-frame/#path), [`format`](/mcp/render-frame/#format) (`png`, `jpeg` or `heic`) and [`max_width`](/mcp/render-frame/#max_width) (16 to 8192 pixels). |
| What's drawn | [`burn_in_timecode`](/mcp/render-frame/#burn_in_timecode), [`ungraded`](/mcp/render-frame/#ungraded), [`sdr_version`](/mcp/render-frame/#sdr_version) and [`selection`](/mcp/render-frame/#selection). |
| Scopes | [`waveform`, `parade` and `histogram`](/mcp/render-frame/#waveform-parade-and-histogram), [`vectorscope` and `vectorscope_zoom`](/mcp/render-frame/#vectorscope-and-vectorscope_zoom). Each scope also writes a JSON file beside the image. |

The switches in the **View** menu never reach this tool, so an agent asks for those pictures here, whatever a person has switched on.

It returns an image and a text. The text gives the moment and the sizes, and its last sentence is "Written to `<path>`." Before that sentence it can add what each scope measured, or a note about:

- A JPEG that flattened a transparent canvas onto black.
- A [graphic](/mcp/render-frame/#graphic-problems-in-the-answer) that warned or failed.
- A recorded cursor that couldn't be drawn.
- A clip with Remove Background [whose masks weren't ready](/mcp/render-frame/#waiting-for-cutout-masks) after 30 seconds, which is drawn uncut.

With a nest open, it renders that nest, at its own canvas and from its own zero. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). An HDR project has its own rules for each format. See [Frames from an HDR project](/mcp/render-frame/#frames-from-an-hdr-project).

## `export`

Puts the timeline on the Export Queue and returns at once, as **File ▸ Export…** (<kbd>⌘E</kbd>) does with its sheet. It takes everything on the sheet but the frame rate. An export runs at the project's rate, or at 12.5 fps for `gif` and 25 fps for `apng`. An agent's export and a menu export go through the same exporter. See [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/).

`preset` and `path` are required.

| To set | Use |
| --- | --- |
| The encoding | [`preset`](/mcp/export/#presets): `h264`, `hevc`, `hevc_alpha`, `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `vp9_alpha_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`, `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav`, `audio_aiff`, `gif` or `apng`. |
| The file | [`path`](/mcp/export/#path-handling). The folder must exist, and an existing file is replaced. |
| What's written | [`size`](/mcp/export/#size) and [`range`](/mcp/export/#range). |
| The picture | [`video_bitrate`](/mcp/export/#exact-bitrates), [`dynamic_range`](/mcp/export/#dynamic-range), [`encoder_speed`](/mcp/export/#encoder-speed) and [`burn_in_timecode`](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
| The sound | [`audio_bitrate`](/mcp/export/#exact-bitrates), [`loudness_lufs`](/mcp/export/#the-loudness-report), [`peak_dbtp`](/mcp/export/#peak-dbtp), [`audio_bits`](/mcp/export/#audio-bits) and [`stems`](/mcp/export/#stems). |

It returns `{export_id, path, status}` at once, and `status` is `queued` or `running`. Jobs run one at a time, and the queue window isn't opened. The export always writes the whole project, even with a nest open. Follow it with [`export_status`](#export_status) and stop it with [`cancel_export`](#cancel_export). The `export_id` lasts until Frame Job quits.

A problem with the request comes back from this call as an error, before anything is queued. A failure while writing comes back from `export_status`. See [Refusals and failures](/mcp/export/#refusals-and-failures).

In the [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/), Frame Job asks you before each `export` runs, naming the file it would write or replace. A client connected over MCP isn't asked.

## `export_status`

Says how an export is going. It's the job's row in **Window ▸ Export Queue**, read now. It never waits, so call it again after a pause until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` returned, 1 or more. |

Every result has `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed`, the seconds since `export` was called, or up to the finish once it has finished. The rest depends on `status`:

| Status | Adds |
| --- | --- |
| `queued` | `waiting`, the queue row's text, while the job waits for memory behind other AV1 and VP9 exports. |
| `queued` or `running` | `estimated_seconds` on `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`. |
| `running` | `progress`, 0 to 1, and `phase` while the exporter names one, such as the loudness measurement. |
| `done` | What the file holds: its size, the settings used, the `loudness` measured, and any `graphic_warnings` and `cursor_warnings`. |
| `failed`, `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's text. |

[Export status](/mcp/export/#export-status) lists every key of a `done` result, and [The loudness report](/mcp/export/#the-loudness-report) explains `loudness`.

Only ids that `export` returned since Frame Job launched are known, so a job a person put on the queue can't be read. Any other id gives an error. A finished job's result outlives its queue row, so it still reads after **Remove** or **Clear Finished**.

## `cancel_export`

Stops an export, as **Cancel** in its Export Queue row does. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` returned, 1 or more. |

A queued export is cancelled before it starts. A running one stops and its half-written file is removed, though the result may still read `running` until the writer has stopped, when `export_status` reads `cancelled`. A finished export is left alone.

It returns what `export_status` returns, and gives an error for an id `export` didn't return since launch.

## Related

- [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/)
- [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/)
- [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)
- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)

| Scopes | [`waveform`, `parade` and `histogram`](/mcp/render-frame/#waveform-parade-and-histogram), [`vectorscope` and `vectorscope_zoom`](/mcp/render-frame/#vectorscope-and-vectorscope_zoom). Each scope also writes a JSON file beside the image. |

The switches in the **View** menu never reach this tool, so an agent asks for those pictures here, whatever a person has switched on.

It returns an image and a text. The text gives the moment and the sizes, and its last sentence is "Written to `<path>`." Before that sentence it can add what each scope measured, or a note about:

- A JPEG that flattened a transparent canvas onto black.
- A [graphic](/mcp/render-frame/#graphic-problems-in-the-answer) that warned or failed.
- A recorded cursor that couldn't be drawn.
- A clip with Remove Background [whose masks weren't ready](/mcp/render-frame/#waiting-for-cutout-masks) after 30 seconds, which is drawn uncut.

With a nest open, it renders that nest, at its own canvas and from its own zero. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). An HDR project has its own rules for each format. See [Frames from an HDR project](/mcp/render-frame/#frames-from-an-hdr-project).

## `export`

Puts the timeline on the Export Queue and returns at once, as **File ▸ Export…** (<kbd>⌘E</kbd>) does with its sheet. It takes everything on the sheet but the frame rate. An export runs at the project's rate, or at 12.5 fps for `gif` and 25 fps for `apng`. An agent's export and a menu export go through the same exporter. See [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/).

`preset` and `path` are required.

| To set | Use |
| --- | --- |
| The encoding | [`preset`](/mcp/export/#presets): `h264`, `hevc`, `hevc_alpha`, `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `vp9_alpha_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`, `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav`, `audio_aiff`, `gif` or `apng`. |
| The file | [`path`](/mcp/export/#path-handling). The folder must exist, and an existing file is replaced. |
| What's written | [`size`](/mcp/export/#size) and [`range`](/mcp/export/#range). |
| The picture | [`video_bitrate`](/mcp/export/#exact-bitrates), [`dynamic_range`](/mcp/export/#dynamic-range), [`encoder_speed`](/mcp/export/#encoder-speed) and [`burn_in_timecode`](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
| The sound | [`audio_bitrate`](/mcp/export/#exact-bitrates), [`loudness_lufs`](/mcp/export/#the-loudness-report), [`peak_dbtp`](/mcp/export/#peak-dbtp), [`audio_bits`](/mcp/export/#audio-bits) and [`stems`](/mcp/export/#stems). |

It returns `{export_id, path, status}` at once, and `status` is `queued` or `running`. Jobs run one at a time, and the queue window isn't opened. The export always writes the whole project, even with a nest open. Follow it with [`export_status`](#export_status) and stop it with [`cancel_export`](#cancel_export). The `export_id` lasts until Frame Job quits.

A problem with the request comes back from this call as an error, before anything is queued. A failure while writing comes back from `export_status`. See [Refusals and failures](/mcp/export/#refusals-and-failures).

In the [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/), Frame Job asks you before each `export` runs, naming the file it would write or replace. A client connected over MCP isn't asked.

## `export_status`

Says how an export is going. It's the job's row in **Window ▸ Export Queue**, read now. It never waits, so call it again after a pause until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` returned, 1 or more. |

Every result has `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed`, the seconds since `export` was called, or up to the finish once it has finished. The rest depends on `status`:

| Status | Adds |
| --- | --- |
| `queued` | `waiting`, the queue row's text, while the job waits for memory behind other AV1 and VP9 exports. |
| `queued` or `running` | `estimated_seconds` on `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`. |
| `running` | `progress`, 0 to 1, and `phase` while the exporter names one, such as the loudness measurement. |
| `done` | What the file holds: its size, the settings used, the `loudness` measured, and any `graphic_warnings` and `cursor_warnings`. |
| `failed`, `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's text. |

[Export status](/mcp/export/#export-status) lists every key of a `done` result, and [The loudness report](/mcp/export/#the-loudness-report) explains `loudness`.

Only ids that `export` returned since Frame Job launched are known, so a job a person put on the queue can't be read. Any other id gives an error. A finished job's result outlives its queue row, so it still reads after **Remove** or **Clear Finished**.

## `cancel_export`

Stops an export, as **Cancel** in its Export Queue row does. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` returned, 1 or more. |

A queued export is cancelled before it starts. A running one stops and its half-written file is removed, though the result may still read `running` until the writer has stopped, when `export_status` reads `cancelled`. A finished export is left alone.

It returns what `export_status` returns, and gives an error for an id `export` didn't return since launch.

---
title: "Tools: rendering and export"
description: "The agent tools that render one frame of the timeline, start an export, follow it on the Export Queue and stop it."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These tools turn the timeline into pictures and files. `render_frame` is how an agent sees what it has done, and `export`, `export_status` and `cancel_export` write the finished file.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Save Frame…', 'File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
  keys={['⌥⌘E', '⌘E']}
  tools={['render_frame', 'export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
  needs="A client connected over MCP, or the Assistant tab."
/>

This page is the quick reference. [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/) and [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/) have every argument in full, with what the agent gets back and what to do when a call fails.

Every tool here also takes `project`, the path of an open project. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/). `export_status` and `cancel_export` accept it but don't use it, because an `export_id` belongs to the launch, not to a project. None of the four takes `scope`.

## `render_frame`

Renders one frame of the finished timeline as a picture the model can see and a file on disk. It's drawn the way an export draws it, so it shows what the file will hold at that moment. Use it before and after every edit. It's the same writer as **File ▸ Save Frame…**, so a PNG written here and one saved from the menu are byte-identical. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).

With no arguments, it draws the frame under the playhead at the canvas's size and writes a PNG to a temporary file. Every argument is optional.

| To set | Use |
| --- | --- |
| The moment | [`t`](/mcp/render-frame/#t), in ticks. Default: the playhead. |
| The file | [`path`](/mcp/render-frame/#path), [`format`](/mcp/render-frame/#format) (`png`, `jpeg` or `heic`) and [`max_width`](/mcp/render-frame/#max_width) (16 to 8192 pixels). |
| What's drawn | [`burn_in_timecode`](/mcp/render-frame/#burn_in_timecode), [`ungraded`](/mcp/render-frame/#ungraded), [`sdr_version`](/mcp/render-frame/#sdr_version) and [`selection`](/mcp/render-frame/#selection). |
| Scopes | [`waveform`, `parade` and `histogram`](/mcp/render-frame/#waveform-parade-and-histogram), [`vectorscope` and `vectorscope_zoom`](/mcp/render-frame/#vectorscope-and-vectorscope_zoom). Each scope also writes a JSON file beside the image. |

The switches in the **View** menu never reach this tool, so an agent asks for those pictures here, whatever a person has switched on.

It returns an image and a text. The text gives the moment and the sizes, and its last sentence is "Written to `<path>`." Before that sentence it can add what each scope measured, or a note about:

- A JPEG that flattened a transparent canvas onto black.
- A [graphic](/mcp/render-frame/#graphic-problems-in-the-answer) that warned or failed.
- A recorded cursor that couldn't be drawn.
- A clip with Remove Background [whose masks weren't ready](/mcp/render-frame/#waiting-for-cutout-masks) after 30 seconds, which is drawn uncut.

With a nest open, it renders that nest, at its own canvas and from its own zero. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). An HDR project has its own rules for each format. See [Frames from an HDR project](/mcp/render-frame/#frames-from-an-hdr-project).

## `export`

Puts the timeline on the Export Queue and returns at once, as **File ▸ Export…** (<kbd>⌘E</kbd>) does with its sheet. It takes everything on the sheet but the frame rate. An export runs at the project's rate, or at 12.5 fps for `gif` and 25 fps for `apng`. An agent's export and a menu export go through the same exporter. See [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/).

`preset` and `path` are required.

| To set | Use |
| --- | --- |
| The encoding | [`preset`](/mcp/export/#presets): `h264`, `hevc`, `hevc_alpha`, `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `vp9_alpha_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`, `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav`, `audio_aiff`, `gif` or `apng`. |
| The file | [`path`](/mcp/export/#path-handling). The folder must exist, and an existing file is replaced. |
| What's written | [`size`](/mcp/export/#size) and [`range`](/mcp/export/#range). |
| The picture | [`video_bitrate`](/mcp/export/#exact-bitrates), [`dynamic_range`](/mcp/export/#dynamic-range), [`encoder_speed`](/mcp/export/#encoder-speed) and [`burn_in_timecode`](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
| The sound | [`audio_bitrate`](/mcp/export/#exact-bitrates), [`loudness_lufs`](/mcp/export/#the-loudness-report), [`peak_dbtp`](/mcp/export/#peak-dbtp), [`audio_bits`](/mcp/export/#audio-bits) and [`stems`](/mcp/export/#stems). |

It returns `{export_id, path, status}` at once, and `status` is `queued` or `running`. Jobs run one at a time, and the queue window isn't opened. The export always writes the whole project, even with a nest open. Follow it with [`export_status`](#export_status) and stop it with [`cancel_export`](#cancel_export). The `export_id` lasts until Frame Job quits.

A problem with the request comes back from this call as an error, before anything is queued. A failure while writing comes back from `export_status`. See [Refusals and failures](/mcp/export/#refusals-and-failures).

In the [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/), Frame Job asks you before each `export` runs, naming the file it would write or replace. A client connected over MCP isn't asked.

## `export_status`

Says how an export is going. It's the job's row in **Window ▸ Export Queue**, read now. It never waits, so call it again after a pause until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` returned, 1 or more. |

Every result has `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed`, the seconds since `export` was called, or up to the finish once it has finished. The rest depends on `status`:

| Status | Adds |
| --- | --- |
| `queued` | `waiting`, the queue row's text, while the job waits for memory behind other AV1 and VP9 exports. |
| `queued` or `running` | `estimated_seconds` on `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`. |
| `running` | `progress`, 0 to 1, and `phase` while the exporter names one, such as the loudness measurement. |
| `done` | What the file holds: its size, the settings used, the `loudness` measured, and any `graphic_warnings` and `cursor_warnings`. |
| `failed`, `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's text. |

[Export status](/mcp/export/#export-status) lists every key of a `done` result, and [The loudness report](/mcp/export/#the-loudness-report) explains `loudness`.

Only ids that `export` returned since Frame Job launched are known, so a job a person put on the queue can't be read. Any other id gives an error. A finished job's result outlives its queue row, so it still reads after **Remove** or **Clear Finished**.

## `cancel_export`

Stops an export, as **Cancel** in its Export Queue row does. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` returned, 1 or more. |

A queued export is cancelled before it starts. A running one stops and its half-written file is removed, though the result may still read `running` until the writer has stopped, when `export_status` reads `cancelled`. A finished export is left alone.

It returns what `export_status` returns, and gives an error for an id `export` didn't return since launch.

## Related

- [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/)
- [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/)
- [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)
- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)
